sourceOnlyStories.snippet: India paid $24.4 billion more on crude oil purchases between April and August compared to a year earlier as the spikes in international oil prices raised the import bill by 48% despite a 0.4% decline in volumes, government data showed on Tuesday. The oil price surge amid the war and the uneven flows from the Middle East hiked India’s crude oil import bill to $74.8 billion in April-August, up by 48.4% from the same period last year, per data from the Oil Ministry’s Petroleum Planning and Analysis
sourceOnlyStories.fullContent: India paid $24.4 billion more on crude oil purchases between April and August compared to a year earlier as the spikes in international oil prices raised the import bill by 48% despite a 0.4% decline in volumes, government data showed on Tuesday. The oil price surge amid the war and the uneven flows from the Middle East hiked India’s crude oil import bill to $74.8 billion in April-August, up by 48.4% from the same period last year, per data from the Oil Ministry’s Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell PPAC cited by Indian outlet Business Standard. Total crude oil imports remained basically flat between April and August, slightly dropping by 0.4% to a total of 100.7 million metric tons of crude for the five-month period, down from 101.1 million tons for the same period in 2025, the data showed. India’s crude oil import bill has soared in recent months, due to the reduced oil flows from the Middle East and the high risks to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. The freight rates on the key route from Ras Tanura on Saudi Arabia’s Persian Gulf to India have soared by more than 400% since February 28, when the war began and Iran closed off the Strait of Hormuz. India paid 60% more for crude oil imports in the April-June quarter compared to the same period last year, as the surge in oil prices couldn’t offset slightly lower import volumes. India’s import costs for September are set to be even higher, as international prices hit $100 per barrel for Brent again, and the Indian crude import price has averaged $114.80 a barrel so far this month, according to government data.  The Indian basket of crude oil is the average of a derived basket comprising a sweet-grade benchmark, Dated Brent, and the sour-grade benchmark of the Oman and Dubai average imported by Indian refineries during each month. By Tsvetana Paraskova for Oilprice.com

worldStories.title: 男性不育问题被“严重瞒报与低估”
worldStories.snippet: It's not all on women anymore — doctors do test men for sperm count and motility. But still too few men get checked, possibly due to a misconception that a healthy sex life means healthy sperm. Spoiler: It doesn't.
worldStories.fullContent:
It's not all on women anymore — doctors do test men for sperm count and motility. But still too few men get checked, possibly due to a misconception that a healthy sex life means healthy sperm. Spoiler: It doesn't.

Sperm counts have fallen globally by more than 51% since 1973, and the decline is accelerating. That's according to a 2026 review of studies published in the journal Antioxidants. But men are less likely to get tested than women for infertility.

"Male infertility is understated. It is so huge a problem," said Edidiong Akang, a reproductive biologist at the University of Lagos, Nigeria.

In a study led by Akang and published in the journal Scientific Reports in 2023, he and his colleagues analyzed semen samples from more than 17,000 men and found that the quality of sperm shape and size (known as sperm morphology) had deteriorated by about 50% between 2010 and 2019.

Sperm motility (how well it swims to the female egg) had also dropped significantly — in Nigeria, for example, by 87% in that same period.

And yet, as Akang told DW, the male share of infertility is "grossly underreported" and, as a result, misunderstood.

Male fertility depends on a healthy sperm shape, size, motility, and its concentration and count. The latter is often used as an indication of male fertility because many millions try to reach the egg but only one or few make it. They need to be strong swimmers.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

These factors depend on other, underlying health conditions: Male infertility can be caused by weight gain, stress, poor sleep, smoking, microplastics and cannabis use.

Weight gain in particular effects the testes (also: testicles), which produce sperm and hormones like testosterone.

The testes function best at two degrees centigrade cooler than the rest of the body. Fat raises the temperature, and that can affect the sperm — its concentration, count and motility.

Male sexual health is often overlooked, possibly because men under the age of 40 don't generally have a regular reason to get checked — if you're older than 40, you may get your prostate checked annually. But even a urologist won't check your sperm count unless you ask them.

Women, on the other hand, get a monthly signal — their menstrual cycle — and may be able to infer from that that something is wrong.

A man gets no such natural signals about his fertility until he tries to conceive with a woman. And by then he may be 30 or 40, when some health outcomes are hard to reverse.

Riffat Bibi, a clinical embryologist who has led an IVF laboratory in Pakistan for 17 years, described what men often say on arrival: "Okay, check my wife first."

Sometimes a mother-in-law brings the daughter-in-law, which also suggests that the mother-in-law thinks: It can't be my son's fault.

And some patients "feel sexual activity is equivalent to fertility, which it is not," said Bibi.

Roughly 80% of Bibi's cases now involve a male factor, far above the 50-50 split long assumed, and her laboratory has had to adapt, she said.

They are also seeing this development in IVF (in vitro fertilization) treatment. Sperm has become so poor that nearly all her clients need an embryologist to pick a single sperm and inject it directly into the egg.

But there is another factor than many men don't talk about much: synthetic testosterone — or steroids.

Some men, keen on a muscley body, suppress their own sperm production unknowingly by taking anabolic steroids, a synthetic form of testosterone.

The appeal of anabolic steroids is straightforward, said Harrison Pope, a Harvard Medical School researcher: Steroids enhance athletic performance. A steroid user, who drinks, smokes and skips half of his workouts can outperform a dedicated, clean athlete.

Pope, who has studied steroids for three decades, said "they are highly effective."

But what you gain in athletic performance, you lose in fertility, because an over-supply of testosterone can shut down sperm production.

A healthy body will keep testosterone levels in balance. Too little testosterone can also impede sperm production.

Sperm production can restart if you stop taking testosterone supplements, but Pope said it depends on your age, and much you were taking and for how long.

Occasional steroid users usually regain a "normal" sperm count. The World Health Organization considers a normal sperm count to be about 16 million sperm per milliliter of semen (or higher).

Heavy, long-term steroid users, meanwhile, often do not recover or return to normal sperm production.

Users typically take steroids in cycles – weeks on the drug, followed by a a break to let the body recover. But when Dutch researchers followed 100 men through one cycle of steroids and for a year after, they found two-thirds still had very low sperm counts, some had no sperm at all, and a year later, their counts had still not returned to normal.

Not everyone takes steroids, and yet falling sperm counts still occur. Take India, for example, where Chirag Bhandari, runs the Institute of Andrology and Sexual Health in Jaipur. Bhandari estimates that steroids account for less than 0.1% of the country's falling sperm counts. Overweight, heat-stress and smoking are usually the cause.

If a man is tested early, his sperm count will often return to normal within six to twelve months, both Bhandari and Bibi said. But the longer the problem goes undetected, the less likely that becomes.

worldStories.fullTranslation:
这不再仅仅是女性的问题——医生确实会检测男性的精子数量和活力。但接受检查的男性仍然太少，这可能是由于一种误解，即认为健康的性生活就意味着健康的精子。剧透一下：事实并非如此。

根据2026年发表在《抗氧化剂》（Antioxidants）杂志上的一项研究综述，自1973年以来，全球精子数量下降了51%以上，而且这种下降正在加速。但男性接受不孕不育检测的可能性仍低于女性。

“男性不育被轻描淡写了。这是一个极其严重的问题，”尼日利亚拉各斯大学的生殖生物学家埃迪迪昂·阿康（Edidiong Akang）表示。

在阿康主导并于2023年发表在《科学报告》（Scientific Reports）杂志上的一项研究中，他和同事分析了超过1.7万名男性的精液样本，发现从2010年到2019年间，精子的形态和大小（即精子形态学指标）质量下降了约50%。

精子活力（游向卵子的能力）也显著下降——例如在尼日利亚，同期下降了87%。

然而，正如阿康告诉德国之声（DW）的那样，男性在不育问题中所占的比例被“严重低估与少报”，结果导致了广泛的误解。

男性生育能力取决于健康的精子形态、大小、活力及其浓度和数量。后者通常被用作男性生育能力的指标，因为数以千万计的精子试图接近卵子，但只有一枚或极少数能够成功。它们必须是强健的“游泳健将”。

如需观看此视频，请启用JavaScript，并考虑升级至支持HTML5视频的网络浏览器

这些因素取决于其他潜在的健康状况：男性不育可能由体重增加、压力、睡眠不良、吸烟、微塑料以及使用大麻引起。

尤其是体重的增加会影响睾丸，而睾丸负责产生精子和包括睾酮在内的激素。

睾丸在比身体其余部位低2摄氏度时的功能状态最佳。脂肪会升高温度，进而影响精子——包括其浓度、数量和活力。

男性性健康往往被忽视，可能是因为40岁以下的男性通常没有定期检查的常规理由——如果你超过40岁，可能会每年检查一次前列腺。但即使是泌尿科医生，除非你主动提出要求，否则也不会为你检查精子数量。

另一方面，女性每月都会收到身体信号——即月经周期——并可能据此推断出身体出现了问题。

而男性在尝试与女性受孕之前，根本得不到任何关于其生育能力的天然信号。等到那时，他可能已经30或40岁了，此时一些健康后果已很难逆转。

巴基斯坦一家试管婴儿（IVF）实验室的主管、临床胚胎学家里法特·比比（Riffat Bibi）从事该工作已有17年，她描述了男性到达时经常说的话：“好吧，先给我妻子检查。”

有时是婆婆带着儿媳来，这也表明婆婆心里认为：绝不可能是自己儿子的问题。

比比说，一些患者“觉得性功能正常就等于具备生育能力，其实不然”。

比比指出，在她接触的病例中，大约80%涉及男性因素，远高于长期以来假定的各占50%的比例，她的实验室不得不对此作出调整。

他们在试管婴儿（体外受精）治疗中也看到了这一发展趋势。精子质量已经变得如此之差，以至于她几乎所有的客户都需要胚胎学家挑选单个精子并将其直接注射到卵子中。

但还有一个许多男性不常谈及的因素：合成睾酮——即类固醇。

一些渴望拥有强健肌肉身材的男性，因服用促合成类固醇（一种合成睾酮）而不知不觉地抑制了自身的精子生成。

哈佛医学院研究员哈里森·波普（Harrison Pope）表示，促合成类固醇的吸引力显而易见：类固醇能够增强运动表现。一个吸烟、喝酒、漏掉一半训练的类固醇使用者，其表现可以超过一名刻苦敬业的“自然健美”运动员。

研究类固醇三十年的波普说：“它们非常有效。”

但你在运动表现上所获得的，正是你在生育能力上所失去的，因为过量供应的睾酮会抑制精子生成。

健康的身体会保持睾酮水平的平衡。睾酮过少也会阻碍精子的生成。

如果停止服用睾酮补充剂，精子生成可能会重新开始，但波普表示，这取决于你的年龄、服用剂量以及持续时间。

偶尔使用类固醇的人通常能恢复“正常”精子数量。世界卫生组织认为，正常精子数量约为每毫升精液1600万个（或更高）。

与此同时，长期大量使用类固醇的人往往无法恢复或回到正常的精子生成水平。

使用者通常按周期使用类固醇——连续用药数周，然后停药一段时间让身体恢复。但当荷兰研究人员对100名经历过一个类固醇周期的男性进行为期一年的跟踪调查时，他们发现三分之二的人精子数量仍然极低，有些人甚至完全没有精子，一年后，他们的精子数量仍未恢复正常。

并非每个人都服用类固醇，但精子数量下降的现象依然在发生。以印度为例，奇拉格·班达里（Chirag Bhandari）在斋浦尔经营着一家男科与性健康研究所。班达里估计，在该国精子数量下降的原因中，类固醇所占比例不足0.1%。超重、热应激和吸烟通常才是罪魁祸首。

班达里和比比都表示，如果男性尽早进行检测，其精子数量通常会在6到12个月内恢复正常。但问题被拖延得越久，恢复的可能性就越小。

worldStories.fullContent:
中新网悉尼9月22日电 由中国驻墨尔本总领事馆主办的“中国文化日”活动日前在澳大利亚维多利亚州吉朗学院举行。中国驻墨尔本总领事房新文、驻墨尔本总领馆副总领事刘东源，吉朗学院校长西蒙·扬、吉朗华人协会主席袁茜敏、侨界代表等800余人出席。

房新文在致辞中表示，希望通过“中国文化日”的沉浸式文化互动体验，澳大利亚青少年能够感受中华文化的魅力，以开放包容的心态看待世界不同文明。驻墨尔本总领馆将积极落实全球文明倡议，深化领区对华人文交流合作，推动两地青少年互访。

吉朗市市长孔泰利在视频致辞中积极评价澳中关系发展，高度赞赏中华文化，愿继续促进澳中文化交流，丰富澳大利亚多元文化。

吉朗学院校长西蒙·扬在致辞中表示，这是该校第一次举办如此大规模的中国文化活动，相信将为澳中两国青年搭建加强了解、增进友谊的文化舞台。

活动现场设置了书法、手工、投壶、礼射、诗词拓印、国风服饰体验等14个文化体验区。总领馆还邀请四川艺术代表团参加此次“中国文化日”活动，精彩演出赢得观众阵阵喝彩与掌声。

作为维多利亚州第二大城市，吉朗市拥有深厚的教育底蕴。吉朗学院成立于1861年，是当地最具代表性的学校之一，现有1500余名学生。(完)

financeStories.originalTitle: Oil Prices Reverse Course as Traders Watch US-Iran Diplomacy
financeStories.snippet: Crude oil prices, which had been falling since last week, today reversed course and made gains ahead of a UN General Assembly session that many hope will yield some progress on peace talks between the U.S. and Iran. financeStories.fullContent: Crude oil prices, which had been falling since last week, today reversed course and made gains ahead of a UN General Assembly session that many hope will yield some progress on peace talks between the U.S. and Iran. As indicated by the latest oil price move, not everyone shares that hope, with Brent crude trading at 101.69 per barrel at the time of writing, and West Texas Intermediate at $93.38 per barrel. However, some observers see oil’s change of direction differently. “The move higher in WTI and the stronger open in Brent have the appearance of a typical short-covering bounce after the recent decline, rather than a fundamental shift,” KCM Trade chief market analyst Tim Waterer said, as quoted by Reuters. “Traders who were positioned for further downside are taking some risk off the table while the diplomatic narrative plays out,” he added. On the other hand, ING commodity analysts said in a note that oil traders remain generally bullish. In a note from Monday, they reported that speculative market players had ramped up their long positions on Brent by 16,904 in the week to September 15, to a total of 282,657, which was the highest since May this year. “The increase was driven largely by short covering as investors continue to price in greater upside risk from Middle East supply disruptions,” Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey noted. Meanwhile, the foreign ministers of the G7 group on Monday called on Iran to stop arming the Yemeni Houthis, who have recently stepped up their attacks on Saudi energy and civil infrastructure. “We condemn in the strongest terms the unacceptable continued strikes carried out by the Houthis in Yemen and against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia,” the officials said in a statement. “We call on the Houthis to immediately cease all military actions, all threats and attacks against civilian shipping, and to return to the political process in good faith,” they also said, as quoted by Reuters. By Irina Slav for Oilprice.com
financeStories.fullTranslation:
自上周以来持续下跌的原油价格在今日逆转走势并实现上涨，此时正值联合国大会召开前夕，许多人希望这次会议能在美伊和平谈判方面取得一定进展。正如最新的油价走势所表明的那样，并非所有人都抱有这种希望；截至发稿时，布伦特原油报每桶101.69美元，西德克萨斯中质原油（WTI）报每桶93.38美元。

然而，一些观察人士对原油走势的反转持有不同看法。路透社援引KCM Trade首席市场分析师蒂姆·沃特勒（Tim Waterer）的话称：“WTI的走高以及布伦特原油的强势开盘，看起来更像是近期下跌后典型的空头回补反弹，而非基本面的转变。”他补充道：“在外交互动进一步明朗之前，此前布局看空的交易员正在撤出部分风险头寸。”

另一方面，荷兰国际集团（ING）大宗商品分析师在一份报告中表示，原油交易员总体上仍持看涨态度。在周一的一份报告中，他们指出，在截至9月15日的一周内，投机性市场参与者增持了16,904手布伦特原油多头头寸，总持仓量达到282,657手，创下今年5月以来的最高水平。沃伦·帕特森（Warren Patterson）和埃瓦·曼特海（Ewa Manthey）指出：“这一增长主要是由空头回补推动的，因为投资者仍在消化中东供应中断带来的更大上行风险。”

与此同时，七国集团（G7）外长周一呼吁伊朗停止向也门胡塞武装提供武器，后者最近加大了对沙特能源和民用基础设施的袭击力度。路透社援引相关官员在一份声明中的表述称：“我们以最强烈的措辞谴责胡塞武装在也门境内及针对沙特阿拉伯王国持续发动的不可接受的袭击。”他们还表示：“我们呼吁胡塞武装立即停止一切军事行动、停止针对民用航运的一切威胁与袭击，并真诚地重返政治进程。”

文/伊琳娜·斯拉夫（Irina Slav）发自Oilprice.com

financeStories.stance: 国际资本与华尔街视角
financeStories.source: CNBC Markets (CNBC 市场官方英文)
financeStories.snippet: Very little is known about which Chinese business executives, if any, are expected to attend.
financeStories.fullContent:
BEIJING — With two days to go before Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to land in the U.S., very little is known about which Chinese executives will join him.

China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs did not immediately respond to a CNBC request for comment Tuesday morning. Late on Monday, the ministry confirmed Xi's U.S. trip, planned for Wednesday to Friday.

On the U.S. side, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella is one of the executives who will attend a dinner expected Thursday in Washington, D.C., according to a source familiar.

Microsoft and the White House did not immediately respond to a CNBC request for comment.

Senior U.S. officials have shared names of some other executives who will join:

Those business leaders include:

On the Chinese side, Reuters reported last week that business representatives under consideration included those from electric car giant BYD, smartphone company Xiaomi, battery makers CATL and Gotion, consumer electronics manufacturer Hisense, automotive parts company Wanxiang, state-owned Bank of China and agricultural conglomerate COFCO Group.

BYD had no comment when contacted by CNBC. The other Chinese companies did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

As tensions between the U.S. and China have escalated in recent years, both governments have put companies from the other country on blacklists that restrict business activity.

—CNBC's Jordan Novet and Ashlee Trujillo contributed to this report.

financeStories.fullContent: With 17% of Qatar's LNG export capacity disabled and Gulf shipments disrupted, buyers arrived at Gastech looking for gas from somewhere else. Organizers valued the agreements announced or advanced in Bangkok at an estimated $60 billion, including a 20-year U.S. LNG contract and a 35-year production agreement in the Gulf of Thailand, while proposed projects in Argentina, Timor-Leste and Tanzania drew interest from buyers and investors. Energy prices pulled back sharply on Monday, with oil falling below $100 per barrel for the first time in two weeks after U.S. President Donald Trump indicated he is open to a potential meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian at the upcoming United Nations General Assembly in New York, scheduled to kick off on Tuesday. Trump is due to address the General Assembly on the opening day while his Iranian counterpart is set to speak on Wednesday. Qatar's North Field and Iran's South Pars occupy the same 9,000-square-kilometer gas formation, which holds 25% of the world's gas resources and supplies 10% of global production. Strikes damaged production and processing facilities on both sides, cutting Qatar's LNG export capacity and reducing the gas available to Iran's domestic market. Related Hormuz Blockage Puts Qatar's $83 Billion LNG Bet at Risk The March strikes damaged two LNG production units at Ras Laffan, cutting Qatar's export capacity by roughly 17%. WoodMac estimates that total repair costs for Qatari gas-processing capacity will hit $5.8 billion, with full repairs on damaged liquefaction trains expected to take up to three years. QatarEnergy recently pushed back the launch of the first production unit at the North Field East project to the first half of 2027, while force majeure declarations on contracted supplies for certain buyers were extended into November 2026. Qatar exported more than 80 million tonnes of LNG in 2025, with India receiving 11.9 mt, Taiwan 8.2 mt while Europe accounted for 11% of total supply. Restrictions on shipping and exports reduced Qatar's hydrocarbon GDP by 25.8% year on year in the first quarter of 2026, pulling the overall economy down 7%. "Qatar is managing US$5.8 billion in repairs and recovery timelines of up to twelve months while commissioning the largest LNG expansion programme in the world," WoodMac's Alexandre Araman said. "That timing matters because 54 mmtpa of uncontracted Qatari volumes will reach the market by 2035, and buyers are making long-term security decisions right now. What this conflict has done is turn a well-understood geographical concentration risk into an operational reality across the entire value chain, from wellhead to export terminal." The situation is just as dire in Iran, with the country having lost roughly a third of its gas capacity following the conflict. Pre-existing hurdles such as international sanctions limiting access to foreign technology, specialized equipment, and skilled workers have compounded the post-war reconstruction burden for the South Pars field, leaving Tehran struggling to meet domestic demand and export goals. At the Bangkok conference, China Gas Holdings unveiled a 20-year liquefied natural gas LNG sales and purchase agreement SPA with U.S. exporter Venture Global LNG to supply 0.5 million tonnes per annum MTPA of LNG starting in 2030. The LNG will be sourced from Venture Global's export projects in Louisiana, expanding China Gas's geographical diversification away from traditional regional pipelines. At the same conference, PETRONAS, PTTEP JDA and the Malaysia-Thailand Joint Authority formalized a 35-year production-sharing contract and gas sales agreement in the Malaysia-Thailand Joint Development Area MTJDA, extending it past the previous expiration date of April 20, 2029. The gas block spans approximately 3,494 square kilometers in the southern Gulf of Thailand and generates 300 million to 400 million standard cubic feet of natural gas per day from fields like Cakerawala, Bumi, and Suriya, split equally between Malaysia and Thailand. Speakers at the event also highlighted renewed interest in projects in Argentina, East Timor and Tanzania, with the Southeast Asian nation announcing plans for two new greenfield LNG plants. Timor-Leste Energy Minister Francisco da Costa Monteiro told Reuters that the country plans two greenfield LNG plants a 5-million-tonne-a-year facility supplied by the long-delayed Greater Sunrise fields and a 1.5-million-tonne plant using remaining gas from Bayu-Undan. By Alex Kimani for Oilprice.com
financeStories.fullTranslation:
随着卡塔尔17%的液化天然气（LNG）出口产能瘫痪以及波斯湾航运受阻，全球买家纷纷涌向天然气大会（Gastech），寻求其他天然气替代来源。主办方估计，在曼谷会议期间宣布或推进的协议总价值约为600亿美元，其中包括一项为期20年的美国LNG合同，以及泰国湾一项为期35年的生产协议；与此同时，阿根廷、东帝汶和坦桑尼亚拟建的项目也吸引了买家与投资者的浓厚兴趣。周一能源价格大幅回落，在油价两周来首次跌破每桶100美元之前，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，他对在即将于纽约开幕的联合国大会期间与伊朗总统马苏德·佩泽希齐扬举行潜在会晤持开放态度（该大会定于周二开幕）。特朗普定于开幕当天在联大发表演讲，而伊朗总统则计划于周三发言。

卡塔尔的北方气田（North Field）与伊朗的南帕尔斯气田（South Pars）同属于一个面积达9000平方公里的天然气构造，蕴藏着全球25%的天然气资源，并供应全球10%的产量。袭击破坏了双方的生产与加工设施，削减了卡塔尔的LNG出口能力，并减少了伊朗国内市场的天然气供应量。

【相关阅读：霍尔木兹海峡封锁危及卡塔尔830亿美元的LNG豪赌】

今年3月的袭击破坏了拉斯拉凡（Ras Laffan）的两个LNG生产单元，使卡塔尔的出口能力削减了大约17%。伍德麦肯兹（WoodMac）估计，卡塔尔天然气加工设施的总维修成本将达到58亿美元，受损液化生产线的全面修复预计最长需要三年时间。卡塔尔能源公司（QatarEnergy）近期已将北方气田东扩（North Field East）项目的首个生产单元投产时间推迟至2027年上半年，同时针对部分买方合同供应所宣布的不可抗力声明已延长至2026年11月。卡塔尔在2025年出口了超过8000万吨LNG，其中印度接收了1190万吨，中国台湾地区接收了820万吨，欧洲则占其总供应量的11%。航运和出口受限导致卡塔尔2026年第一季度油气行业GDP同比下降25.8%，拖累整体经济下滑7%。

“卡塔尔一方面在应对高达58亿美元的维修费用以及长达12个月的恢复周期，另一方面还在推进全球规模最大的LNG扩产计划，”伍德麦肯兹的亚历山大·阿拉曼（Alexandre Araman）表示，“这一时间节点至关重要，因为到2035年将有5400万吨/年未签署合同的卡塔尔天然气进入市场，而买家目前正在做出关乎长期能源安全的关键决策。这场冲突所带来的结果，是将众所周知的地理集中度风险，转变成了从井口到出口终端整条价值链上的现实运营挑战。”

伊朗的局势同样严峻，该国在冲突爆发后失去了大约三分之一的天然气产能。既有的阻碍（如限制获取外国技术、专用设备及技术工人的国际制裁）加剧了南帕尔斯气田战后重建的负担，导致德黑兰在满足国内需求与出口目标方面举步维艰。

在曼谷大会上，中国燃气控股有限公司（China Gas Holdings）公布了一份为期20年的液化天然气购销协议（SPA），该协议与美国出口商Venture Global LNG签署，将从2030年开始每年供应50万吨（MTPA）LNG。这些LNG将来自Venture Global在路易斯安那州的出口项目，从而扩大了中国燃气在传统区域管道之外的地理多元化布局。

在同一场会议上，马来西亚国家石油公司（PETRONAS）、泰国国家石油勘探生产公司（PTTEP JDA）以及马来西亚-泰国联合管辖局正式签署了马泰联合开发区（MTJDA）为期35年的产量分成合同及天然气销售协议，将其延期至原定的2029年4月20日到期日之后。该天然气区块横跨泰国湾南部约3494平方公里的海域，通过Cakerawala、Bumi和Suriya等气田每日生产3亿至4亿标准立方英尺的天然气，由马来西亚和泰国均分。

与会发言人还重点指出了市场对阿根廷、东帝汶和坦桑尼亚项目的重新关注，其中东帝汶宣布了建设两座全新绿地LNG工厂的计划。东帝汶能源部长弗朗西斯科·达科斯塔·蒙泰罗（Francisco da Costa Monteiro）向路透社表示，该国计划建设两座绿地LNG工厂：一座年产能500万吨的设施将由拖延已久的大日出气田（Greater Sunrise）供应原料，另一座年产能150万吨的工厂将利用巴尤-温丹气田（Bayu-Undan）的剩余天然气。

文/Alex Kimani，Oilprice.com

financeStories.originalTitle: Study: Young users (9 to 18Y) ditch Google for AI, with unknown consequences
financeStories.fullContent:
School researchers reviewed nearly 200 studies on how artificial intelligence affects children and young people’s ability to learn and think. They found that we know very little about how AI use impacts younger school children.

Researchers wanted to find out how AI tools affect students' critical thinking and problem-solving abilities. They analysed 173 international studies that had looked at the use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in school and education.

Storrøsæter has analysed 173 international research articles on the use of generative artificial intelligence (machine learning techniques where the goal is not only to analyse data, but also to create new data, for example in the form of text, images, audio, video or programming code. The most widespread use of generative AI is through chatbots, such as ChatGPT) in school work and education. Her study was conducted with a group of colleagues from Czech universities.

The goal of the literature review was to find out whether AI tools strengthen or weaken children and youths’ ability to think critically and solve problems independently. Many people believe that these skills have never been more important than now, in the 21st century.

“The most important finding is that AI in and of itself does not make us any better or worse at thinking. It’s easy to believe that the tools will either strengthen or weaken learning. We found a clear dual effect. The same technology can do both,” said Storrøsæter, who is also a geographer and teacher who focuses on subject-matter pedagogy.

“The study confirms the dual nature of AI. The same technology can have both constructive and destructive effects. We were surprised that this came across so clearly,” says Hilde Storrøsæter, a PhD research fellow at NTNU’s Department of Teacher Education. Photo: NTNU SHOW MORE

AI tools support important skills when they are used to challenge, ask questions, compare different viewpoints and build one’s own line of reasoning.

“But when AI becomes a shortcut to a ready-made answer, the chance of overdependence, more superficial thinking and weakened independent problem solving increases,” Storrøsæter says.

The Norwegian Media Authority’s survey (in Norwegian) on the media habits of 9 to 18-year-olds shows that the use of Google searches fell from 72% in 2024 to 47% in 2026 for this age group.

The report shows that 39% of Norwegian 11 to 12-year-olds use AI.

The website ung.no – Norway’s online information and communication channel for young people aged 13 to 20 – is also losing traffic because young people are switching to AI tools to find answers to their questions. The number of visits to ung.no fell from 24 million to 18 million from 2024 to 2025. Google’s new AI summaries have also influenced the decline in traffic.

The researchers analysed studies from 2022 – the year that AI language models swept onto the world stage – and up to the spring of 2025. Few predicted the power and speed with which technology would change society. AI affects how information is created, used, shared and disseminated. The consequences are particularly significant in schools and educational settings.

The education sector has already been shaped by AI. The question is whether we can shape the use of AI.

Research on the use of AI in education should provide direction for pedagogy, policy and research in the field to help authorities and other institutions make decisions on AI use.

Storrøsæter and her colleagues uncovered three major gaps in what we know about AI use.

In 80% of the studies the researchers analysed, the participants were university or college students. This means that we know surprisingly little about the academic and cognitive effects of AI use on children and youths, at a time while they are still developing how they perceive, process and evaluate information.

“We can’t simply assume that what applies to a 22-year-old university student also applies to a 10- or 14-year-old,” says Storrøsæter.

“If AI takes over the thinking process before pupils have had time to develop their own skills for critical thinking and problem solving, the consequences could be completely different for them than for adults,” she says.

You might also like: “We must develop thinkers. Not crammers and fact-experts”

Most of the articles in the literature review are based on self-reporting. This is considered a less reliable method than objective studies of changes over time.

The school researchers also uncovered a geographically skewed distribution in where the studies were done. South Asia, Southeast Asia and East Asia – primarily China – dominate with 28 studies. In Europe, Spain and the United Kingdom led with nine studies each.

A total of 15 studies were conducted in the USA. Africa, South America and Central Asia are seriously underrepresented. This creates a research gap that should be addressed.

Overall, the studies show positive effects more often than negative ones.

The researchers behind the new literature review highlight three crucial issues in particular: How AI tools are used, teachers’ understanding of AI, and the demands teachers place on students and pupils.

“Teacher education has a dual task. We have to educate teachers who can use and relate critically to AI themselves. At the same time, our education students should also be able to teach children and young people how to use AI. It is not enough to just teach them to use some AI tools,” says Storrøsæter.

For us to succeed with AI in schools, teacher education has to succeed.

“Students need to understand what technology does to the learning process itself, such as what happens when AI solves parts of the task. Which parts of the thinking process are important for the pupils to still do themselves? How do we design tasks where AI becomes a tool, and not a replacement, for thinking?”

Storrøsæter is not worried about students’ or pupils’ use of AI in and of itself.

“I support being restrictive in terms of not using AI with very young pupils. But when AI is used, it has to happen on the teacher’s terms,” she says.

If AI is used uncritically, you don’t build any skills with it, and you miss out on a lot of learning situations. This will only increase disparities between those who use AI critically and as a tool, and those who use it uncritically simply to complete a task faster. If that happens, schools and universities will both face significant challenges.

Technology will probably continue to develop faster than we can put curricula and regulations in place. Our number one task is therefore to cultivate AI literacy, by protecting and developing competence in critical thinking, problem solving, source criticism and the ability to make independent assessments.

“The education sector is already strongly influenced and shaped by AI. The question is whether we can shape the use of AI so that it supports students’ thinking instead of taking it over.”

Storrøsæter stresses that if we are to succeed with AI in schools, teacher education has to succeed.

Reference: Tomáš Bendl, Lenka Krajňáková, Hilde Storrøsæter, Emil Drápela, Martin Hanus: Dual Nature of GenAI: Catalyst or Barrier for Critical Thinking and Problem-Solving Skills? A systematic Review, Journal of Information Technology Education: Research • Volume 25 • 2026 • https://doi.org/10.28945/5834

教育学者回顾了近200项关于人工智能如何影响儿童和青少年学习与思考能力的研究。他们发现，对于人工智能的使用究竟如何影响低龄学童，我们知之甚少。

研究人员希望了解人工智能工具如何影响学生的批判性思维与解决问题的能力。他们分析了173项探讨生成式人工智能（GenAI）在学校和教育中应用的国际研究。

斯托罗塞特（Storrøsæter）分析了173篇关于生成式人工智能（一种机器学习技术，其目标不仅是分析数据，还包括生成新数据，例如文本、图像、音频、视频或编程代码形式；生成式人工智能最广泛的应用形式是聊天机器人，例如ChatGPT）在学业和教育中应用的国际研究论文。她的这项研究是与来自捷克多所大学的同事共同开展的。

这项文献综述的目标，是探究人工智能工具究竟会增强还是削弱儿童和青少年批判性思考以及独立解决问题的能力。许多人认为，在21世纪的当下，这些技能比以往任何时候都更加重要。

“最重要的发现是，人工智能本身并不会让我们在思考上变得更好或更差。人们很容易认为这些工具要么增强学习，要么削弱学习。但我们发现了一种明显的双重效应。同一项技术可能产生这两种完全不同的效果，”斯托罗塞特说道，她同时也是一名专注于学科教学法的地理学者与教师。

“这项研究证实了人工智能的双重特性。同一项技术既能产生建设性效果，也能产生破坏性影响。这种现象表现得如此鲜明，让我们感到惊讶，”挪威科技大学（NTNU）教师教育系博士后研究员希尔德·斯托罗塞特（Hilde Storrøsæter）表示。图片来源：NTNU 展开更多

当人工智能工具被用于提出挑战、发起质疑、对比不同观点以及构建个人论证逻辑时，它们能够对重要技能提供支持。

“但当人工智能变成获取现成答案的捷径时，过度依赖、思维浅层化以及独立解决问题能力削弱的风险就会上升，”斯托罗塞特表示。

挪威媒体管理局针对9至18岁人群媒体习惯的调查显示，在这一年龄段中，使用谷歌搜索的比例从2024年的72%骤降至2026年的47%。

该报告显示，39%的挪威11至12岁儿童使用人工智能。

面向13至20岁青少年的挪威在线信息与沟通渠道——网站 ung.no，其访问量也出现了下滑，原因是年轻人正在转向人工智能工具来寻找问题答案。ung.no的访问量从2024年的2400万次下滑至2025年的1800万次。谷歌最新推出的人工智能摘要功能同样对流量的下滑产生了影响。

研究人员分析了从2022年（人工智能语言模型席卷全球舞台的年份）至2025年春季的研究。很少有人预料到这项技术改变社会的力量与速度。人工智能影响了信息的创建、使用、共享和传播方式。这种后果在学校和教育环境中尤为显著。

教育领域已经被人工智能所重塑。核心问题在于我们是否能够引导和塑造人工智能的使用。

关于人工智能在教育中应用的研究应当为该领域的教学法、政策与学术研究指明方向，以帮助主管当局和其他机构就人工智能的使用做出决策。

斯托罗塞特及其同事揭示了当前我们对人工智能使用认知的三个主要空白。

在研究人员分析的文献中，80%的研究对象为大学或学院学生。这意味着，当儿童和青少年仍在发展他们感知、处理和评估信息的能力时，我们对人工智能使用带给他们的学业与认知影响知之甚少，令人惊讶。

“我们不能简单地假定适用于22岁大学生的结论同样适用于10岁或14岁的孩子，”斯托罗塞特表示。

“如果人工智能在学生尚未来得及培养出自己的批判性思维和解决问题能力之前就接管了思考过程，那么对其产生的后果可能与对成年人完全不同，”她说道。

您可能还喜欢：“我们必须培养思考者，而不是死记硬背者和事实专家”

文献综述中的大部分文章均基于自我报告数据。相比于跨时间变化的长周期客观研究，这种方法被认为可靠性较低。

教育学者们还揭示了研究开展地域分布上的不均衡。南亚、东南亚和东亚（主要是中国）以28项研究占据主导。在欧洲，西班牙和英国各以9项研究领先。

在美国共开展了15项研究。非洲、南美洲和中亚地区的代表性严重不足。这就造成了一个亟待填补的研究空白。

总体而言，研究显示的积极影响多于消极影响。

新文献综述背后的研究人员特别强调了三个关键议题：人工智能工具的具体使用方式、教师对人工智能的理解，以及教师对中小学生提出的要求。

“教师教育肩负着双重任务。我们必须培养出自身能够使用并批判性对待人工智能的教师。与此同时，我们的师范生还应当有能力教会儿童和青少年如何使用人工智能。仅仅教他们使用某些人工智能工具是远远不够的，”斯托罗塞特表示。

为了使人工智能在学校教育中取得成功，教师教育必须首先取得成功。

“学生需要理解这项技术对学习过程本身造成了什么影响，例如当人工智能解决了一部分任务时会发生什么。思考过程中的哪些部分是仍然必须由学生自己完成的关键环节？我们该如何设计作业任务，使人工智能成为思考的工具，而不是替代思考的工具？”

斯托罗塞特本身并不担心学生使用人工智能这件事本身。

“我支持对极低龄学童采取限制使用人工智能的做法。但当人工智能被使用时，必须在教师设定的规则与要求下进行，”她表示。

如果缺乏批判性地使用人工智能，你无法凭借它构建任何技能，而且会错失大量的学习情境。这只会加剧两极分化：一边是批判性地将人工智能作为工具使用的人，另一边则是为了更快完成任务而盲目使用的人。若这种情况发生，学校和大学都将面临巨大挑战。

技术的演进速度可能仍将快于我们制定课程体系和监管政策的速度。因此，我们的首要任务是培养人工智能素养，通过保护和发展批判性思维、解决问题、信源甄别以及做出独立评估的能力来筑牢根基。

“教育领域已经深受人工智能的影响与塑造。现在的关键在于，我们是否能够引导和塑造人工智能的使用，使其支持而不是取代学生的思考。”

斯托罗塞特（Storrøsæter）强调，如果我们想在学校成功推广人工智能，教师教育必须率先取得成功。

参考文献：Tomáš Bendl, Lenka Krajňáková, Hilde Storrøsæter, Emil Drápela, Martin Hanus: 《生成式人工智能的双重属性：批判性思维与解决问题能力的催化剂还是绊脚石？系统性文献综述》（Dual Nature of GenAI: Catalyst or Barrier for Critical Thinking and Problem-Solving Skills? A systematic Review），载于《信息技术教育研究杂志》（Journal of Information Technology Education: Research）• 第25卷 • 2026年 • https://doi.org/10.28945/5834

接受减肥减重手术后，人体吸收酒精的速度会快得多。患者在选择所需的手术类型时必须了解这一点。

在挪威西北海岸附近的罗弗敦群岛上空，一架救援直升机正盘旋在一艘游轮上方。片刻后，两名人员和一个大包被降送至甲板。随后，一根缆绳被抛向紧挨在一旁的海岸警卫队巡逻舰。游轮已做好受拖航准备。幸运的是，这只是一次测试新装备的演习，而非真实的紧急情况。

当你年仅11岁且患有注意力缺陷多动障碍（ADHD），却被期望像其他人一样按部就班完成学业时，那会是怎样的一种体验？

In 80% of the studies the researchers analysed, the participants were university or college students.

Storrøsæter has analysed 173 international research articles on the use of generative artificial intelligence... in school work and education. Her study was conducted with a group of colleagues from Czech universities.

consensus: 生成式AI已深度渗透青少年的信息获取和学习场景，传统搜索与部分公共青年平台流量明显下滑。
生成式AI具有工具双重性：既可作为提问和对比观点的认知催化剂，也可因充当现成答案捷径而削弱独立批判性思维。
现有关于AI对学习影响的研究存在明显样本偏倚，绝大多数聚焦于高等教育阶段的学生。

financeStories.title: 我说“不”，苹果却说“要”
financeStories.originalTitle: I said no and Apple said yes
financeStories.fullContent:
Tuesday 22 Sept 2026 Play Synthesised Audio

The nice thing about keeping a blog is that I can say at precisely 9:51am, Wednesday 5th February 2025, I discovered that macOS 15.3 had enabled a feature that was phoning home every 15 minutes with personal data. And that I said “no” and turned it off.

At the time Apple were generous enough to provide a setting to disable this feature.

macOS 15 Apple Intelligence setting.

Although they hid the second part deeper, because why should saying “no” be easy?

macOS 15 Apple Intelligence privacy setting.

Last week I succumbed to Apple’s harassment and upgraded macOS 15 to 27. I only skipped one major version, Apple skipped 10!

And today I discovered that Apple had removed the “no” switch.

The “AI” industry has many flaws, the word “consent” being seemingly missing from training data and company handbooks is one of them. AI bros do not take “no” for an answer. When Apple advertised their deepfake feature back in June it became obvious Apple does not “think different.”

Digging through macOS 27 settings I turned off Siri (again). Of course, multiple unkillable Siri processes remain, stealing memory and writing data. For what purpose? Who knows. Note that they removed “Apple Intelligence” from this control.

macOS 27 Siri setting.

All of this garbage was enabled after upgrading to macOS 27 despite me having “Apple Intelligence & Siri” turned off already. That was a rather explicit “no”, no?

The icing on this cake is the 22.28 GB brick clogging my disk space.

macOS 27 Apple Intelligence accounting for 22.28 GB.

Apple is charging £500/TB on new MacBooks so that is what, £11 they’ve stolen from me?

But that’s a trivial cost compared to the consent problem. The AI industrial complex does not do consent. You will use it. You cannot look away, it will be stuffed down your throat and if you say “no” they’ll cut out your tongue.

The AI industry is vile. My AI policy tried to list my concerns but it’s hopelessly outdated. I can’t keep up. Here’s just three of many headlines I collected this month:

The list is endless. There is no limit to the human toll to keep this bubble inflated.

Call me a radical but I’ve chosen not to kowtow to billionaires. Do you want another Epstein list? Because this is how you create another Epstein list. Fund a generation of psychopaths building on a foundation of non-consent and privacy invasion. Fantastic idea!

AI bros keep telling me “just turn it off” and when I do they remove the choice.

All opinions are my own and not those of a large language model. Everything I write is one hundred percent human. Because I care!

I founded Valley Fold to help you, so let’s make your website happen. Whether you have requirements scoped or you’re lost for ideas, we can work with you at any stage.

2026年9月22日，星期二 播放合成音频

写博客的一大好处在于，我可以准确记录下：2025年2月5日星期三上午9点51分，我发现macOS 15.3启用了一项每15分钟就会将个人数据传回服务器的功能。当时我说“不”，并把它关掉了。

那时苹果还算慷慨，提供了一个可以禁用该功能的设置项。

macOS 15 Apple Intelligence设置。

尽管他们把第二部分藏得更深——毕竟，说“不”怎么能那么容易呢？

macOS 15 Apple Intelligence隐私设置。

上周，我向苹果不断的骚扰妥协，将macOS 15升级到了27。我只跳过了一个大版本，苹果却直接跳过了10个！

而今天我发现，苹果已经把那个说“不”的开关给移除了。

“AI”行业存在诸多缺陷，训练数据和公司手册中似乎彻底缺失了“知情同意”（consent）这个词，便是其中之一。AI狂热者绝不接受拒绝。当苹果在6月份大肆宣传其深度伪造（deepfake）功能时，很显然苹果早已不再“非同凡想”（Think Different）。

翻遍macOS 27的设置，我（再次）关掉了Siri。当然，后台依然残留着多个无法杀死的Siri进程，占用着内存并不停写入数据。究竟出于什么目的？天晓得。注意，他们已经从这个控制项中移除了“Apple Intelligence”。

macOS 27 Siri设置。

尽管我此前已经关闭了“Apple Intelligence与Siri”，但在升级到macOS 27后，所有这些垃圾功能全被自动启用了。那明明是一个相当明确的拒绝，不是吗？

更糟糕的是，还有一个重达22.28 GB的“大砖头”死死霸占着我的磁盘空间。

macOS 27 Apple Intelligence占用了22.28 GB。

苹果新款MacBook的存储扩容收费高达每TB 500英镑，这么算来，他们等于从我这里偷走了11英镑？

但与“知情同意”问题相比，这点金钱代价根本微不足道。AI复合体从来不管什么知情同意。你必须使用它。你避无可避，它会被硬塞进你的喉咙；如果你敢说“不”，他们就会割掉你的舌头。

AI行业令人作呕。我的AI政策曾试图列出我的担忧，但如今它已彻底过时。我根本跟不上。以下是我本月收集的众多新闻头条中的三则：

这样的名单无休无止。为了维持这个泡沫的膨胀，所付出的人力代价没有任何底线。

随便你们说我激进好了，但我选择不向亿万富翁们卑躬屈膝。你们想要另一份爱泼斯坦名单吗？因为这正是制造下一份爱泼斯坦名单的温床。资助一群建立在“违背意愿”和“侵犯隐私”基础上的精神变态者，真是绝妙的主意！

AI狂热者老是对我说“关掉它不就行了”，而当我真的去关时，他们却直接把选择权给剥夺了。

所有观点均代表我个人，而非出自大型语言模型。我写下的每一个字都百分之百出自人类之手。因为我在乎！

我创办Valley Fold是为了帮助大家，让我们一起把你的网站做起来吧。无论你已经有了明确的需求范围，还是完全毫无头绪，我们都能在任何阶段与你展开合作。

In my previous blog post I mention I use to travel far and frequently and describe the gear I take with me to make it a more pleasant experience. Unfortunately not every place I visit offers the same kind and levels of freedoms I got used to growing up in a liberal democracy 🇪🇺.

To be completely honest, that by itself doesn’t usually limit my perceived freedoms much1, unrestricted internet access though might not always be possible without some kind of workaround and in this article I’m going to show you the ones I usually put in place to circumvent such restrictions.

By default I ignore the DNS resolvers offered by e.g. DHCP and use one of the freely available wildly known, usually Cloudflare’s. Setting one up in my minirouter2 means that’s going to be transparent for every other device connecting to my private LAN. Some provider allows for extra privacy like DNS over TLS and I recommend to turn it on because it generally comes with no perceivable extra latency, so why not?

This simple change by itself doesn’t help against filtered IP blocks or ports but it’s already useful in avoiding a series of other annoyances and, most importantly, it’s a fire-and-forget kind of configuration change that makes it a no brainer.

For years I’ve been a happy customer of Proton services and I can’t recommend them enough: they offer a simple and cost effective way to get rid of annoying ads-infested Google services while getting a big boost in privacy, there’s a free plan too so you can start for free and pay for the pro services only once you feel the need, like I did.

One problem I have with this is that it won’t let me choose the country on the exit side of the VPN. That’s reasonable for a free service but it might not help in solving the blocking/filtering problem if the exit country is also applying filters. More in general the quality of service might be degraded because of overloaded servers, so all in all is mostly hit and miss and I can’t rely on that as a stable solution.

There are more reasons why I want to be able to choose where the VPN exit point is located, for example some streaming platform might restrict or show different available content based on the geographical position of the source IP address, and so on.

I hear you: why not to pay for the pro ProtonVPN service too, or any of the many other VPN services out there? I could but it would be mostly a waste of money given that my need for a VPN connection is very spotty and never accounts for more than a few hours per month at worst.

What if I could just boot a pro VPN server on demand, pay only for the hours I use it and even choose in which region of the world it runs?

What I do when custom DNS and ProtonVPN aren’t helping is simple enough: I just spin up a WireGuard server with a single CLI command, connect my WireGuard clients to it as full tunnel, tear it down once I’m done with another CLI command.

Simple, fast, effective, and very cheap:

All I need to do is to copy (once) the printed WireGuard configuration into e.g. my Macbook’s WireGuard client and enable that to tunnel all the network traffic via the new VPN instance.

You can find the implementation in this repository hosted on my forge, it should be usable out of the box assuming you have OpenTofu5 installed and an AWS account to use.

The module doesn’t do much as you can see, I list the gist of it here for the ones who aren’t interested in the code:

Most of the default configuration values can be changed, refer to variables.tf for more details.

If for whatever reason you don’t want to use AWS, it should be relatively easy to (ask a coding agent to) modify the module to use your favorite provider instead, like Digital Ocean or else, and spin up the instance there instead.

The module has also a feature switch that lets me create a CNAME DNS record into my l3x.in zone that I host at Njalla but you can consider that as an implementation detail and use a different provider for that too, or simply ignore the extra DNS record and use the public EC2 DNS hostname directly; the repository is meant to be used as a blueprint more than a one-size-fits-all solution.

I’m sure many other valid solutions, like the ones offered by Tailscale, exist. I still prefer to bake my own and avoid creating yet another account / install other software on my workstation when the effort is relatively low.

For Tailscale in particular I find myself in this funny situation by which I admire their offering and at the same time I never feel like I need them because I can simply get away with just some WireGuard and iptables.

Most notably… where’s the fun going to be otherwise?

I hope you have found this helpful, as usual I’m looking forward to get your feedback, see /contact to get in touch with me.

Disclaimer: I don’t make use of any LLM help for writing my blog posts and this one is no exception.

Keep on rockin’ in the Free World Internet 🤘

applying for visas is still a pain though, especially here in South East Asia where I’m living right now ↩

see previous article about my travel setup ↩

I currently pay them US$83.76 for 24 months, so ~3.5USD/month ↩

or Terraform… but you should really use OpenTofu ↩

by default in the eu-south-1 (Italy) region ↩

you can cut this latency down sensibly if you are willing to ignore upgrading out-of-date OS packages, refer to https://forge.l3x.in/alex/aws-ec2-vpn/src/branch/master/cloud-init.yaml.tftpl for details ↩
financeStories.fullTranslation:
在我之前的博文中，我提到过我经常长途旅行，并介绍了随身携带的装备，正是它们让旅途体验更加愉快。遗憾的是，并非我到访的每个地方都能提供与我在自由民主国家🇪🇺成长过程中所习惯的同等种类和程度的自由。

坦白说，仅这一点本身通常并不会对我有感知的自由造成太大限制¹；然而，如果不采取某种变通方法，不受限制的互联网访问可能并非总能实现。在本文中，我将向大家展示我通常用来绕过此类限制的方案。

默认情况下，我会忽略 DHCP 等提供的 DNS 解析器，转而使用公开可用且广为人知的服务之一，通常是 Cloudflare 的。在我的便携微型路由器²中设置一个解析器，意味着对连接到我专用局域网的每台其他设备来说，这一过程都是透明无感的。有些提供商支持额外的隐私保护功能，例如 DNS over TLS，我建议开启它，因为通常它不会带来任何肉眼可见的额外延迟，何乐而不为呢？

单凭这一简单的改动并不能解决 IP 地址段或端口被过滤的问题，但它在避免一系列其他烦心事方面已经非常管用。最重要的是，这是一种一劳永逸式的配置更改，完全无需费神操作。

多年来，我一直是 Proton 服务的忠实用户，对其赞不绝口：他们提供了一种简单且极具成本效益的方式，既能摆脱令人厌烦且充斥广告的谷歌服务，又能大幅提升隐私安全性。他们还提供免费套餐，因此你可以免费起步，等到真正觉得有需要时再升级购买专业服务，就像我当时那样。

我对该服务唯一不满的一点在于：它不允许我自由选择 VPN 出口端的国家。对于一项免费服务来说这合情合理，但如果出口端国家本身也在实施网络过滤，这可能就无法解决屏蔽/过滤的问题了。更普遍的情况是，由于服务器过载，服务质量可能会有所下降，因此总体而言好坏全碰运气，我无法将其视作一种稳定的解决方案。

我想自主选择 VPN 出口节点所在位置的原因还不止于此，例如，某些流媒体平台可能会根据源 IP 地址的地理位置来限制内容或展示不同的可用内容，诸如此类。

我明白你想问什么：为什么不顺便购买 ProtonVPN 的付费专业版，或者市面上其他众多的 VPN 服务呢？我确实可以买，但鉴于我对 VPN 连接的需求非常零散，最极端情况下一个月加起来也用不上几个小时，买它基本上纯属浪费钱。

如果我能按需随时启动一台专业级 VPN 服务器，只需为使用的具体时长付费，甚至还能自主选择它在世界哪个地区运行，岂不美哉？

当自定义 DNS 和 ProtonVPN 都派不上用场时，我的做法其实很简单：只需运行一条 CLI 命令即可快速启动一台 WireGuard 服务器，将我的 WireGuard 客户端以全隧道模式连接到它，使用完毕后再运行另一条 CLI 命令将其销毁。

简单、迅速、高效且极其便宜：

我所需做的就是将打印出的 WireGuard 配置（一次性）复制到例如我的 MacBook 的 WireGuard 客户端中，并启用它，以便将所有网络流量通过这台全新的 VPN 实例进行隧道传输。

你可以在我代码托管平台上托管的这个代码仓库中找到具体实现。假定你已经安装了 OpenTofu⁵ 并且拥有可用的 AWS 账号，那么它应该可以开箱即用。

正如你所见，该模块并没有做太多复杂的事，在此我为那些对代码不感兴趣的人列出其核心要点：

大多数默认配置值都可以更改，详情请参考 variables.tf。

如果出于某种原因你不想使用 AWS，那么（让编程 AI 助手来）修改该模块以使用你喜欢的其他提供商（如 Digital Ocean 等）并改在那里启动实例，应该相对容易。

该模块还有一个功能开关，允许我在我托管于 Njalla 的 l3x.in 区域中创建一条 CNAME DNS 解析记录，但你可以将其视作一个实现细节，并在该环节使用其他提供商，或者直接忽略这条额外的 DNS 记录而直接使用 EC2 的公开 DNS 主机名；该代码仓库更倾向于用作蓝图参考，而非放之四海皆准的现成解决方案。

我确信存在许多其他切实可行的方案，比如 Tailscale 提供的方案。但我仍然更倾向于自己动手搭建，并且在所需精力相对较低的情况下，避免为了使用某项服务再去创建一个账号或在我的工作站上安装多余的软件。

特别是对于 Tailscale，我发现自己处于这样一种微妙的处境：我欣赏他们提供的产品，但与此同时我从未觉得非用他们不可，因为我只需借助少许 WireGuard 和 iptables 就能轻松搞定。

最值得一提的是……要是不这么折腾，乐趣又何在呢？

希望这篇文章对你有所帮助，与往常一样，我非常期待收到你的反馈，可通过 /contact 与我取得联系。

financeStories.title: 男性不育问题被“严重瞒报与低估”
financeStories.snippet: It's not all on women anymore — doctors do test men for sperm count and motility. But still too few men get checked, possibly due to a misconception that a healthy sex life means healthy sperm. Spoiler: It doesn't.
financeStories.fullContent:
It's not all on women anymore — doctors do test men for sperm count and motility. But still too few men get checked, possibly due to a misconception that a healthy sex life means healthy sperm. Spoiler: It doesn't.

Sperm counts have fallen globally by more than 51% since 1973, and the decline is accelerating. That's according to a 2026 review of studies published in the journal Antioxidants. But men are less likely to get tested than women for infertility.

"Male infertility is understated. It is so huge a problem," said Edidiong Akang, a reproductive biologist at the University of Lagos, Nigeria.

In a study led by Akang and published in the journal Scientific Reports in 2023, he and his colleagues analyzed semen samples from more than 17,000 men and found that the quality of sperm shape and size (known as sperm morphology) had deteriorated by about 50% between 2010 and 2019.

Sperm motility (how well it swims to the female egg) had also dropped significantly — in Nigeria, for example, by 87% in that same period.

And yet, as Akang told DW, the male share of infertility is "grossly underreported" and, as a result, misunderstood.

Male fertility depends on a healthy sperm shape, size, motility, and its concentration and count. The latter is often used as an indication of male fertility because many millions try to reach the egg but only one or few make it. They need to be strong swimmers.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

These factors depend on other, underlying health conditions: Male infertility can be caused by weight gain, stress, poor sleep, smoking, microplastics and cannabis use.

Weight gain in particular effects the testes (also: testicles), which produce sperm and hormones like testosterone.

The testes function best at two degrees centigrade cooler than the rest of the body. Fat raises the temperature, and that can affect the sperm — its concentration, count and motility.

Male sexual health is often overlooked, possibly because men under the age of 40 don't generally have a regular reason to get checked — if you're older than 40, you may get your prostate checked annually. But even a urologist won't check your sperm count unless you ask them.

Women, on the other hand, get a monthly signal — their menstrual cycle — and may be able to infer from that that something is wrong.

A man gets no such natural signals about his fertility until he tries to conceive with a woman. And by then he may be 30 or 40, when some health outcomes are hard to reverse.

Riffat Bibi, a clinical embryologist who has led an IVF laboratory in Pakistan for 17 years, described what men often say on arrival: "Okay, check my wife first."

Sometimes a mother-in-law brings the daughter-in-law, which also suggests that the mother-in-law thinks: It can't be my son's fault.

And some patients "feel sexual activity is equivalent to fertility, which it is not," said Bibi.

Roughly 80% of Bibi's cases now involve a male factor, far above the 50-50 split long assumed, and her laboratory has had to adapt, she said.

They are also seeing this development in IVF (in vitro fertilization) treatment. Sperm has become so poor that nearly all her clients need an embryologist to pick a single sperm and inject it directly into the egg.

But there is another factor than many men don't talk about much: synthetic testosterone — or steroids.

Some men, keen on a muscley body, suppress their own sperm production unknowingly by taking anabolic steroids, a synthetic form of testosterone.

The appeal of anabolic steroids is straightforward, said Harrison Pope, a Harvard Medical School researcher: Steroids enhance athletic performance. A steroid user, who drinks, smokes and skips half of his workouts can outperform a dedicated, clean athlete.

Pope, who has studied steroids for three decades, said "they are highly effective."

But what you gain in athletic performance, you lose in fertility, because an over-supply of testosterone can shut down sperm production.

A healthy body will keep testosterone levels in balance. Too little testosterone can also impede sperm production.

Sperm production can restart if you stop taking testosterone supplements, but Pope said it depends on your age, and much you were taking and for how long.

Occasional steroid users usually regain a "normal" sperm count. The World Health Organization considers a normal sperm count to be about 16 million sperm per milliliter of semen (or higher).

Heavy, long-term steroid users, meanwhile, often do not recover or return to normal sperm production.

Users typically take steroids in cycles – weeks on the drug, followed by a a break to let the body recover. But when Dutch researchers followed 100 men through one cycle of steroids and for a year after, they found two-thirds still had very low sperm counts, some had no sperm at all, and a year later, their counts had still not returned to normal.

Not everyone takes steroids, and yet falling sperm counts still occur. Take India, for example, where Chirag Bhandari, runs the Institute of Andrology and Sexual Health in Jaipur. Bhandari estimates that steroids account for less than 0.1% of the country's falling sperm counts. Overweight, heat-stress and smoking are usually the cause.

If a man is tested early, his sperm count will often return to normal within six to twelve months, both Bhandari and Bibi said. But the longer the problem goes undetected, the less likely that becomes.

Edited by: Zulfikar Abbany
financeStories.fullTranslation:
这不再仅仅是女性的问题——医生确实会检测男性的精子数量和活力。但接受检查的男性仍然太少，这可能是由于一种误解，即认为健康的性生活就意味着健康的精子。剧透一下：事实并非如此。

根据2026年发表在《抗氧化剂》（Antioxidants）杂志上的一项研究综述，自1973年以来，全球精子数量下降了51%以上，而且这种下降正在加速。但男性接受不孕不育检测的可能性仍低于女性。

“男性不育被轻描淡写了。这是一个极其严重的问题，”尼日利亚拉各斯大学的生殖生物学家埃迪迪昂·阿康（Edidiong Akang）表示。

在阿康主导并于2023年发表在《科学报告》（Scientific Reports）杂志上的一项研究中，他和同事分析了超过1.7万名男性的精液样本，发现从2010年到2019年间，精子的形态和大小（即精子形态学指标）质量下降了约50%。

精子活力（游向卵子的能力）也显著下降——例如在尼日利亚，同期下降了87%。

然而，正如阿康告诉德国之声（DW）的那样，男性在不育问题中所占的比例被“严重低估与少报”，结果导致了广泛的误解。

男性生育能力取决于健康的精子形态、大小、活力及其浓度和数量。后者通常被用作男性生育能力的指标，因为数以千万计的精子试图接近卵子，但只有一枚或极少数能够成功。它们必须是强健的“游泳健将”。

如需观看此视频，请启用JavaScript，并考虑升级至支持HTML5视频的网络浏览器

这些因素取决于其他潜在的健康状况：男性不育可能由体重增加、压力、睡眠不良、吸烟、微塑料以及使用大麻引起。

尤其是体重的增加会影响睾丸，而睾丸负责产生精子和包括睾酮在内的激素。

睾丸在比身体其余部位低2摄氏度时的功能状态最佳。脂肪会升高温度，进而影响精子——包括其浓度、数量和活力。

男性性健康往往被忽视，可能是因为40岁以下的男性通常没有定期检查的常规理由——如果你超过40岁，可能会每年检查一次前列腺。但即使是泌尿科医生，除非你主动提出要求，否则也不会为你检查精子数量。

另一方面，女性每月都会收到身体信号——即月经周期——并可能据此推断出身体出现了问题。

而男性在尝试与女性受孕之前，根本得不到任何关于其生育能力的天然信号。等到那时，他可能已经30或40岁了，此时一些健康后果已很难逆转。

巴基斯坦一家试管婴儿（IVF）实验室的主管、临床胚胎学家里法特·比比（Riffat Bibi）从事该工作已有17年，她描述了男性到达时经常说的话：“好吧，先给我妻子检查。”

有时是婆婆带着儿媳来，这也表明婆婆心里认为：绝不可能是自己儿子的问题。

比比说，一些患者“觉得性功能正常就等于具备生育能力，其实不然”。

比比指出，在她接触的病例中，大约80%涉及男性因素，远高于长期以来假定的各占50%的比例，她的实验室不得不对此作出调整。

他们在试管婴儿（体外受精）治疗中也看到了这一发展趋势。精子质量已经变得如此之差，以至于她几乎所有的客户都需要胚胎学家挑选单个精子并将其直接注射到卵子中。

但还有一个许多男性不常谈及的因素：合成睾酮——即类固醇。

一些渴望拥有强健肌肉身材的男性，因服用促合成类固醇（一种合成睾酮）而不知不觉地抑制了自身的精子生成。

哈佛医学院研究员哈里森·波普（Harrison Pope）表示，促合成类固醇的吸引力显而易见：类固醇能够增强运动表现。一个吸烟、喝酒、漏掉一半训练的类固醇使用者，其表现可以超过一名刻苦敬业的“自然健美”运动员。

研究类固醇三十年的波普说：“它们非常有效。”

但你在运动表现上所获得的，正是你在生育能力上所失去的，因为过量供应的睾酮会抑制精子生成。

健康的身体会保持睾酮水平的平衡。睾酮过少也会阻碍精子的生成。

如果停止服用睾酮补充剂，精子生成可能会重新开始，但波普表示，这取决于你的年龄、服用剂量以及持续时间。

偶尔使用类固醇的人通常能恢复“正常”精子数量。世界卫生组织认为，正常精子数量约为每毫升精液1600万个（或更高）。

与此同时，长期大量使用类固醇的人往往无法恢复或回到正常的精子生成水平。

使用者通常按周期使用类固醇——连续用药数周，然后停药一段时间让身体恢复。但当荷兰研究人员对100名经历过一个类固醇周期的男性进行为期一年的跟踪调查时，他们发现三分之二的人精子数量仍然极低，有些人甚至完全没有精子，一年后，他们的精子数量仍未恢复正常。

并非每个人都服用类固醇，但精子数量下降的现象依然在发生。以印度为例，奇拉格·班达里（Chirag Bhandari）在斋浦尔经营着一家男科与性健康研究所。班达里估计，在该国精子数量下降的原因中，类固醇所占比例不足0.1%。超重、热应激和吸烟通常才是罪魁祸首。

班达里和比比都表示，如果男性尽早进行检测，其精子数量通常会在6到12个月内恢复正常。但问题被拖延得越久，恢复的可能性就越小。

financeStories.fullContent:
中新网悉尼9月22日电 由中国驻墨尔本总领事馆主办的“中国文化日”活动日前在澳大利亚维多利亚州吉朗学院举行。中国驻墨尔本总领事房新文、驻墨尔本总领馆副总领事刘东源，吉朗学院校长西蒙·扬、吉朗华人协会主席袁茜敏、侨界代表等800余人出席。

房新文在致辞中表示，希望通过“中国文化日”的沉浸式文化互动体验，澳大利亚青少年能够感受中华文化的魅力，以开放包容的心态看待世界不同文明。驻墨尔本总领馆将积极落实全球文明倡议，深化领区对华人文交流合作，推动两地青少年互访。

吉朗市市长孔泰利在视频致辞中积极评价澳中关系发展，高度赞赏中华文化，愿继续促进澳中文化交流，丰富澳大利亚多元文化。

吉朗学院校长西蒙·扬在致辞中表示，这是该校第一次举办如此大规模的中国文化活动，相信将为澳中两国青年搭建加强了解、增进友谊的文化舞台。

活动现场设置了书法、手工、投壶、礼射、诗词拓印、国风服饰体验等14个文化体验区。总领馆还邀请四川艺术代表团参加此次“中国文化日”活动，精彩演出赢得观众阵阵喝彩与掌声。

作为维多利亚州第二大城市，吉朗市拥有深厚的教育底蕴。吉朗学院成立于1861年，是当地最具代表性的学校之一，现有1500余名学生。(完)

financeStories.title: 苹果首个现场音乐场馆即将于其英国总部地下落成开放
financeStories.originalTitle: Apple’s first live music venue is opening beneath its UK headquarters
financeStories.snippet: The venue is opening below Battersea Power Station, also well recognized for featuring on the cover of Pink Floyd’s Animals album. | Image: Apple Apple is preparing to open a new "state-of-the-art" live music venue in the UK, a 600-capacity space for hosting performances, recording sessions, and video broadcasts. The venue, called Apple Music Hall, is located underneath Apple's European headquarters in London's iconic Battersea Power Station, and is set to open next week on September 28th. Detai
financeStories.fullContent: Apple is preparing to open a new “state-of-the-art” live music venue in the UK, a 600-capacity space for hosting performances, recording sessions, and video broadcasts. The venue, called Apple Music Hall, is located underneath Apple’s European headquarters in London’s iconic Battersea Power Station, and is set to open next week on September 28th. Details about the opening show have yet to be announced. “Apple’s deep love for music dates all the way back to the very beginning, from the launch of the iPod to the long-running iTunes Music Festival to the debut of Apple Music,” said Oliver Schusser, Apple’s vice president of Apple Music and International Content. “Today, with the opening of Apple Music Hall, we are once again taking an unprecedented step further in our commitment to artists and fans by supporting live music in ways only Apple can do.” [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Hall-event-space-01.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Hall-event-space-02.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Hall-foyer-angle-02.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] The limited capacity and layout is “designed intentionally to close the gap between intimacy and production value,” according to Apple’s announcement, with seating that feels close to the performer while providing artists with a 38-foot-wide stage that can be reconfigured to their needs. Apple Music Hall has a 48-speaker spatial sound system positioned around the audience, is hardwired for 16 or more broadcast cameras, and includes two dedicated recording and mixing studios behind the stage that allow it to operate as a full production facility. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Radio-greenroom.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Radio-VIP-greenroom.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Radio-A-list-corridor.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Radio-greenroom-hair-makeup.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] The performance space is opening alongside new Apple Music radio studios in Battersea, with Apple announcing that all of its London-based hosts and shows will now broadcast from the facility. “We’re always looking for new opportunities to connect the artists and the fans because we are fans,” said Apple Music’s global creative director, Zane Lowe. “Great music and memories will be made at Apple Music Hall.” [Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_srDnNd9iaE] Apple Music Hall marks the company’s return to London’s music scene, having previously run the iTunes Music Festival in England’s capital city for a decade — hosting acts like One Direction, Lady Gaga, Elton John, and Adele at intimate local venues — before its cancellation in 2017. Battersea Power Station, a decommissioned Art Deco facility that reopened in 2022, also has its own roots in music history, having appeared on the cover of Pink Floyd’s Animals album.
financeStories.fullTranslation:
苹果公司正准备在英国开设一个全新的“尖端”现场音乐场馆。这是一个可容纳600人的空间，用于举办演出、录音以及视频转播。该场馆名为“Apple Music Hall”，位于苹果欧洲总部所在地——伦敦标志性建筑巴特西发电站（Battersea Power Station）的地下，定于下周9月28日正式开放。首场演出的详细信息尚未公布。

苹果公司负责 Apple Music 及国际内容业务的副总裁奥利弗·舒塞尔（Oliver Schusser）表示：“苹果对音乐的热爱可一路追溯到最开端，从 iPod 的推出，到长期举办的 iTunes 音乐节，再到 Apple Music 的亮相。今天，随着 Apple Music Hall 的开幕，我们再次迈出了前所未有的一步，以只有苹果才能做到的方式支持现场音乐，践行我们对艺术家和乐迷的承诺。”

[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Hall-event-space-01.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Hall-event-space-02.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Hall-foyer-angle-02.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

据苹果官方公告，有限的容纳人数和场地布局是“特意为了拉近亲近感与制作水准之间的距离而设计”。观众席让人感觉与表演者近在咫尺，同时为艺术家提供了一个38英尺宽、可根据其需求重新布局的舞台。Apple Music Hall 围绕观众配备了由48个扬声器组成的空间音频系统，预先布线支持16台或更多转播摄像机，并在后台设有两个专门的录音和混音工作室，使其能够作为一个功能齐全的制作中心运转。

[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Radio-greenroom.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Radio-VIP-greenroom.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Radio-A-list-corridor.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Radio-greenroom-hair-makeup.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

该演出空间与巴特西的新 Apple Music 电台演播室一同启用。苹果宣布，其常驻伦敦的所有主持人及节目今后都将从该设施进行播出。“我们一直在寻找新的机会来连接艺术家和歌迷，因为我们自己也是乐迷，”Apple Music 全球创意总监赞恩·洛（Zane Lowe）说，“伟大的音乐和回忆将在 Apple Music Hall 诞生。”

[Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_srDnNd9iaE]

Apple Music Hall 标志着该公司重返伦敦音乐界。此前，苹果曾在这座英国首都举办过长达十年的 iTunes 音乐节——在当地亲密的小型场馆中邀请了单向组合（One Direction）、Lady Gaga、埃尔顿·约翰（Elton John）和阿黛尔（Adele）等知名艺人表演，该音乐节于2017年停办。巴特西发电站是一处停运的装饰艺术风格工业建筑，于2022年重新开放，它在音乐史上也拥有深厚渊源，曾登上平克·弗洛伊德（Pink Floyd）乐队《Animals》专辑的封面。

financeStories.title: gzip 能充当语言模型吗？
financeStories.originalTitle: Can gzip be a language model?
financeStories.fullContent:
A while back I wrote about language modeling without neural networks, where I generated Shakespeare with an unbounded n-gram model: no weights, no training, just counting. Fortuitously, I came across the paper Language Modeling is Compression, which mentioned the compression–prediction equivalence:

every prediction model is inherently a compressor, and all compression algorithms are prediction models.

This led to the natural question: can gzip do language modeling?1 No neural network, no learned parameters, nothing. Just the compressor that ships with your operating system. You prime it with a corpus, give it a normal text prompt, and it continues that prompt by searching for the byte sequences that compress best. Here’s some real, unedited output after priming it on tiny Shakespeare:

It turns out, kind of? It’s not exactly coherent text, but it clearly knows something about the text. Much more than I expected gzip to know.2 So how can a compressor generate this?

Think about what a compressor does. It spends few bytes on data it “expects” and many bytes on data it doesn’t. If I hand you a file that’s the letter A repeated a million times, you can describe it in one sentence. A million random bytes, on the other hand, have no structure to exploit and barely compress at all.

This is not a coincidence; it’s the core of information theory. The number of bits needed to encode a symbol is $-\log_2 p$, where $p$ is the probability the model assigns to it. High probability means few bits. So any compressor has a probability model hiding inside it, whether or not anyone wrote one down.

gzip uses DEFLATE, which compresses the next bytes by finding matches against the recent text in a 32 KiB sliding window. If a continuation echoes something already in the window, DEFLATE encodes it as a cheap back-reference instead of literal bytes. So:

A continuation that gzip “expected”, because it echoes text already in its window, compresses to almost nothing.

That gives us a score. If I have some context and I want to know how good a candidate continuation is, I just measure:

The smaller the compressed length, the more “predicted” the candidate is. To prime the model, I include a corpus in gzip’s window. Any continuation that looks like the corpus compresses small, and any continuation that doesn’t compresses large.

Scoring is one thing; generating is another. The naive approach of picking the single next byte that compresses best fails badly, and for a subtle reason: gzip only gives an integer byte length (no fractions). Adding one byte often doesn’t change the compressed length at all, so many candidates tie and the signal is buried in quantization noise.

The fix is to look ahead a whole span before committing. gzipt runs a beam search over byte sequences. At each step, the current context is:

Then gzipt tries possible next bytes. Each candidate continuation is scored by compressing context + candidate and checking how many bytes the compressed result takes.

One detail that matters is that only the last tail bytes of generated output stay in the scoring context. DEFLATE codes nearby matches more cheaply than far ones, so if gzip could see its entire history, the cheapest thing to do is often to fall into verbatim loops, repeatedly copying text it just emitted.

You can see the decoding and scoring process in the animation above, which is the same replay shown at the top. The whole thing is one file of pure standard-library Python (just zlib). Code’s on GitHub if you want to play with it.

The paper did try this, but it ended up performing poorly. Adding beam search significantly improved generation quality (an idea they mentioned), which is discussed below. ↩︎

The code actually uses zlib instead of spawning a gzip process, but the name GziPT was too good. I believe they both use the same DEFLATE algorithm under the hood. ↩︎
financeStories.fullTranslation:
前段时间我写过一篇关于无需神经网络进行语言建模的文章，当时我用一个无界 n-gram 模型生成了莎士比亚风格的文本：没有权重，没有训练，仅仅是计数。机缘巧合下，我看到了论文《语言建模即压缩》（Language Modeling is Compression），其中提到了压缩与预测的等价性：
每一个预测模型本质上都是一个压缩器，而所有压缩算法也都是预测模型。
这引出了一个很自然的问题：gzip 能用来做语言建模吗？¹ 不需要神经网络，没有学习得到的参数，什么都没有。就用你操作系统自带的压缩工具。你先用一个语料库对其进行预热（prime），给它一个常规的文本提示词，然后它通过搜索压缩效果最好的字节序列来续写该提示词。以下是在用微型莎士比亚（tiny Shakespeare）语料库预热后，生成的真实且未经编辑的输出：
结果表明，似乎还真行？虽然它算不上完全连贯的文本，但显然对文本是有所了解的。这远远超出了我对 gzip 认知能力的预期。² 那么，压缩器究竟是如何生成这些内容的呢？
不妨想一想压缩器在做什么。对于它“预期中”的数据，它只需花费很少的字节；而对于它“未曾预期”的数据，则要消耗很多字节。如果我递给你一个重复了一百万次字母 A 的文件，你用一句话就能描述它。相反，一百万个随机字节则没有任何可利用的结构，几乎完全无法压缩。
这绝非巧合，而是信息论的核心所在。对一个符号进行编码所需的比特数为 $-\log_2 p$，其中 $p$ 是模型赋予它的概率。概率越高意味着所需的比特数越少。因此，任何压缩器内部都隐藏着一个概率模型，无论是否有人显式写出过它。
gzip 采用的是 DEFLATE 算法，它通过在 32 KiB 的滑动窗口中查找与近期文本匹配的内容来压缩后续字节。如果续写内容呼应了窗口中已有的内容，DEFLATE 就会将其编码为低开销的后向引用，而不是原样输出字面量字节。因此：
一个 gzip “预期中”的续写——因为它呼应了其窗口中已有的文本——几乎可以被压缩至忽略不计。
这就为我们提供了一个评分标准。如果我有一些上下文，想要知道某个候选续写有多好，我只需要测量：
压缩后的长度越小，说明该候选续写被“预测”的程度越高。为了预热模型，我将一个语料库放入 gzip 的窗口中。任何看起来像该语料库的续写内容，压缩后体积都很小；而任何不像它的内容，压缩后体积都很大。
评分是一回事，生成则是另一回事。直接选取压缩效果最好的下一个字节这种朴素方法彻底失败了，原因很微妙：gzip 只给出整数形式的字节长度（没有小数分值）。添加一个字节往往根本不会改变压缩后的长度，因此许多候选续写会打成平手，有效信号被淹没在量化噪声中。
解决办法是在最终确定前向前看完整的一个跨度（span）。gzipt 对字节序列执行束搜索（beam search）。在每一步中，当前的上下文为：
接着 gzipt 会尝试可能的下一个字节。通过压缩“上下文 + 候选续写”并检查压缩结果占用多少字节，来对每个候选续写进行评分。
一个关键细节是：生成的输出中只有最后的末尾字节会保留在评分上下文中。DEFLATE 对临近匹配的编码开销比远距离匹配更低，因此如果 gzip 能看到它的全部历史，开销最小的做法往往是陷入逐字死循环，不断重复复制它刚刚吐出的文本。
你可以在上面的动画中看到解码和评分过程，这与顶部展示的回放相同。整个实现是一个纯标准库的 Python 文件（仅使用了 zlib）。如果你想尝试一下，代码已开源在 GitHub 上。
论文中确实尝试过这种方法，但最终表现较差。加入束搜索显著提升了生成质量（这是他们提到过的一个想法），下文对此进行了讨论。↩︎
代码实际上使用的是 zlib 而不是直接调用 gzip 进程，但 GziPT 这个名字实在太贴切了。我相信它们底层使用的都是相同的 DEFLATE 算法。↩︎

financeStories.title: Morphotonics 筹集 4000 万欧元，将其显示技术扩展至数据中心领域
financeStories.originalTitle: Morphotonics raises €40M to expand its display tech into data centers
financeStories.snippet: Deeptech company Morphotonics raises €40M from investors including 3M Ventures, Innovation Industries, BOM, and Invest-NL.
financeStories.fullContent:
The Netherlands’ ASML is possibly the biggest name in lithography, using its machines to etch patterns onto silicon wafers inside a computer chip factory known as a fab. Fellow Dutch company Morphotonics is smaller and works in a different corner of the same field: nanoimprint lithography, or NIL, a process used to manufacture the displays in AR glasses and other optics. It said it has benefited from ASML’s supply chain and uses many of the same vendors.

Morphotonics has spent 12 years developing that technology, largely under the radar. Now, as demand for smart glasses and other optics surges, the company said Tuesday it has raised €40 million to scale up production and push into a new market: optical components for data centers.The round was backed by 3M Ventures, Innovation Industries, BOM, and Invest-NL. The European Innovation Council (EIC) Fund; Ernij Next, a Dutch family office; and the European Investment Bank (EIB) also participated.

Morphotonics’ NIL work means the startup creates a “stamp” and applies it to photosensitive materials to create various kinds of displays, from augmented reality glasses to privacy screens for cars.

This is useful in creating the waveguide technology used in smart glasses, including the Meta Ray-Ban Display, Even Reality, and Magic Leap. Waveguides are thin pieces of glass or plastic that deflect light along a specific path so that they display an image in front of the wearer’s eyes.

Smart glasses are just one application of Morphotonics’ technology, but it’s currently the most in-demand one. This week, China said sales of smart glasses in the country doubled in the first eight months of this year. In June, the market research firm IDC noted that shipments of smart glasses with displays are expected to reach 12.2 million by 2030. As that market grows, manufacturers are looking for machines like Morphotonics’ that can produce those displays at scale.

The latest fundraising is part of an extended round that began in 2024, raised in multiple installments. The company has used the money to more than double its headcount to 60 employees, up from roughly 30 in September 2024, when CEO Hugo Da Silva joined. Morphotonics still plans to hire and expects headcount to stabilize around 70 to 75 people.

“Typically, display manufacturers would acquire our equipment as part of the supply chain, and we integrate it into the entire manufacturing process. We teach them the process, we provide the chemicals, and they can manufacture that,” Da Silva said. The company’s manufacturing is heavily concentrated in Asia, with teams in China, Taiwan, South Korea, and the U.S. “Strong local presence is very important,” he said.

Da Silva said the company’s next machine, currently being built, will be capable of producing more than 6 million waveguides a year. He said it’s expected to start shipping early next year.

Beyond displays, that expansion also includes a push into co-packaged optics, a technology used in data centers that use Photonic Integrated Circuits — chips that use light instead of electricity — to move data between servers and network equipment. The startup hasn’t shipped any machines in this area, but it said customers have validated its tech.

The company sells both hardware machines and the process through licensing to ensure that customers get the best results. Right now, roughly 90% of the startup’s revenue comes from hardware sales, with 10 to 15 systems deployed globally. The company expects to reach 50 deployments in the next two to three years, which should also increase its revenue from services.

荷兰的阿斯麦（ASML）可能是光刻领域最负盛名的企业，其机器被用于在被称为晶圆厂的计算机芯片工厂内将图案蚀刻到硅晶圆上。同为荷兰公司的 Morphotonics 规模相对较小，并在同一领域的另一个细分方向深耕：纳米压印光刻（nanoimprint lithography，简称 NIL），一种用于制造 AR 眼镜及其他光学器件中显示屏的工艺。该公司表示，自身受益于 ASML 的供应链，并且采用了许多相同的供应商。

Morphotonics 花了 12 年时间研发这项技术，在此期间大部分时间都鲜为人知。如今，随着对智能眼镜及其他光学器件的需求激增，该公司周二宣布已筹集 4000 万欧元，用于扩大生产规模并进军一个新市场：数据中心光学组件。本轮融资由 3M Ventures、Innovation Industries、BOM 和 Invest-NL 领投/参投。欧洲创新理事会（EIC）基金、荷兰家族办公室 Ernij Next 以及欧洲投资银行（EIB）也参与了投资。

Morphotonics 的 NIL 业务意味着该初创公司会制作一个“压印模具”，并将其压印于光敏材料上，从而制造各种显示产品，从增强现实眼镜到汽车防窥屏皆涵盖其中。

这对于制造智能眼镜（包括 Meta Ray-Ban Display、Even Reality 和 Magic Leap）所使用的光波导技术非常有用。光波导是轻薄的玻璃或塑料片，能将光线沿特定路径偏转，从而在佩戴者眼前呈现图像。

智能眼镜只是 Morphotonics 技术的应用场景之一，但目前是需求最为迫切的场景。本周，中国方面表示，今年前八个月该国智能眼镜销量翻了一番。今年 6 月，市场研究机构 IDC 指出，到 2030 年，带显示屏的智能眼镜出货量预计将达到 1220 万台。随着这一市场的增长，制造商正在寻找像 Morphotonics 这样能够大规模生产此类显示屏的设备。

最新的这一轮融资始于 2024 年，是一轮分多期筹集的扩展轮融资。公司已利用这笔资金将员工人数增加了一倍多，达到 60 人，而在 2024 年 9 月现任首席执行官雨果·达席尔瓦（Hugo Da Silva）加入时大约只有 30 人。Morphotonics 仍计划继续扩招，预计员工人数将稳定在 70 至 75 人左右。

“通常情况下，显示器制造商会将我们的设备作为其供应链的一部分进行采购，我们则将其集成到整个制造流程中。我们向他们传授工艺，提供化学试剂，他们便可进行生产，”达席尔瓦说。该公司的制造业务高度集中在亚洲，并在中国大陆、中国台湾、韩国和美国设有团队。“拥有强大的本土业务网络非常重要，”他表示。

达席尔瓦透露，公司目前正在制造的下一代设备每年将能够生产超过 600 万套光波导。他表示，预计该设备将于明年初开始出货。

除显示器件外，此次业务扩张还包括进军共封装光学（CPO）领域，这是数据中心中使用的一种技术，通过光子集成电路（PIC，即用光代替电来传输数据的芯片）在服务器与网络设备之间传输数据。这家初创公司尚未在该领域交付任何设备，但表示客户已经验证了其技术。

该公司既销售硬件设备，也通过技术授权提供工艺服务，以确保客户获得最佳效果。目前，该公司约 90% 的收入来自硬件销售，全球已部署了 10 到 15 套系统。该公司预计在未来两到三年内将部署量增加至 50 套，这也将提高其服务收入。

financeStories.originalTitle: MiMo-v2.6-Pro: Intelligence, Performance and Price Analysis
financeStories.fullContent:
Released September 2026

MiMo-V2.6-Pro is amongst the leading models in intelligence and reasonably priced when comparing to other open weight models of similar size. It's also notably fast, however somewhat verbose. The model supports text, image, speech, and video input, outputs text, and has a 1M tokens context window.

MiMo-V2.6-Pro scores 46 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, placing it well above average among comparable models (median: 18). When evaluating the Intelligence Index, it generated 140M tokens, which is somewhat verbose in comparison to the median of 140M.

Pricing for MiMo-V2.6-Pro is $0.43 per 1M input tokens (somewhat expensive, median: $0.30) and $0.87 per 1M output tokens (moderately priced, median: $1.13). In total, it cost $206.66 to evaluate MiMo-V2.6-Pro on the Intelligence Index.

At 125 tokens per second, MiMo-V2.6-Pro is notably fast (75).

This page shows the reasoning version of this model.

A non-reasoning variant may also exist.

Supports: text, image, speech, and video

Metrics are compared against models of the same class:

Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2 includes: AA-Briefcase v1.1, GDPval-AA v2.1, AutomationBench-AA, Terminal-Bench 4.0, SciCode, Humanity's Last Exam, GDP.pdf, CritPt, AA-Omniscience, AA-LCR v1.1. See Intelligence Index methodology for further details, including a breakdown of each evaluation and how we run them.

Indicates whether the model weights are available. Models are labelled as 'Commercial Use Restricted' if commercial use is limited by conditions, and as 'Non-commercial' if the license prohibits commercial use.

Measures the performance of models on specific capabilities and industries

Agentic knowledge work, (Elo-500)/2000

Agentic real-world work tasks, (Elo-500)/2000

Agentic SaaS workflows

Agentic coding & terminal use

Reasoning & knowledge

Professional document reasoning, All-pass

1 - hallucination rate

Long context reasoning

Legal agentic work, criterion pass rate

Agentic business operations

Quantitative analysis on spreadsheets & documents

Kubernetes incident root-cause analysis

Medical long context reasoning

While model intelligence generally translates across use cases, specific evaluations may be more relevant for certain use cases.

AA-Briefcase Elo is a combined metric that aggregates analytical quality Elo, presentation Elo, and rubric pass rate, with rubric performance converted into Elo via synthetic head-to-head matches. Elo and 95% confidence interval bounds are clamped at 0.

AA-Omniscience Index (higher is better) measures knowledge reliability and hallucination. It rewards correct answers, penalizes hallucinations, and has no penalty for refusing to answer. Scores range from -100 to 100, where 0 means as many correct as incorrect answers, and negative scores mean more incorrect than correct.

Weighted average cost per Intelligence Index task. Each evaluation’s cost is calculated from input, cache hit, cache write, reasoning, and answer token prices, divided by task count, and weighted by its Intelligence Index weight.

The number of tokens required per Intelligence Index task. This is calculated by multiplying the output tokens per eval by the relative weights of each benchmark in the Intelligence Index, then dividing by task count (excluding repeats).

The cost to run the evaluations in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, calculated using the model's input, cache hit, cache write, reasoning, and answer token prices and the number of tokens used across evaluations (excluding repeats).

Price per token for cached prompts (previously processed), typically offering a significant discount compared to regular input price, represented as USD per million tokens. The values shown here are the cache hit price; cache write and cache storage are billed separately and vary by provider — see "Cache pricing by provider" for detail.

Larger context windows are relevant to RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) LLM workflows which typically involve reasoning and information retrieval of large amounts of data.

Maximum number of combined input & output tokens. Output tokens commonly have a significantly lower limit (varied by model).

Measured by Output Speed (tokens per second)

Tokens per second received while the model is generating tokens (ie. after first chunk has been received from the API for models which support streaming).

Figures represent performance of the model's first-party API or the median across providers where a first-party API is not available.

The weighted average time (seconds) per Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index task. This is calculated by dividing output tokens per task by output speed, weighted by the relative weights of each benchmark in the Intelligence Index.

Measured by Time (seconds) to First Token

Time to first answer token received, in seconds, after API request sent. For reasoning models, this includes the 'thinking' time of the model before providing an answer. For models which do not support streaming, this represents time to receive the completion.

Seconds to output 500 tokens, calculated based on time to first token, 'thinking' time for reasoning models, and output speed

Seconds to receive a 500 token response. Key components:

The total number of trainable weights and biases in the model, expressed in billions. These parameters are learned during training and determine the model's ability to process and generate responses.

The number of parameters actually executed during each inference forward pass, expressed in billions. For Mixture of Experts (MoE) models, a routing mechanism selects a subset of experts per token, resulting in fewer active than total parameters. Dense models use all parameters, so active equals total.

Common questions about MiMo-V2.6-Pro

MiMo-V2.6-Pro was released on September 21, 2026.

MiMo-V2.6-Pro was created by Xiaomi.

MiMo-V2.6-Pro has a time to first token (TTFT) of 2.34s (based on Xiaomi's API), which is better than average compared to other open weight models of similar size (median: 2.33s).

MiMo-V2.6-Pro costs $0.43 per 1M input tokens (better than average, median: $0.45) and $0.87 per 1M output tokens (very competitive, median: $1.68), based on Xiaomi's API.

financeStories.title: oMLX 创作者兼维护者 Jun Kim 加入 Hugging Face，助力 MLX 社区发展
financeStories.originalTitle: Jun Kim, oMLX creator and maintainer, joins Hugging Face to support the MLX community
financeStories.fullContent:
MLX is Apple's framework for local AI, especially optimized for Apple Silicon. We are big MLX supporters since it was the Christmas present from Awni and Angelos in 2023, and proud that Hugging Face is the Hub where people find MLX models and contribute their own. Usage of open, local AI is accelerating, and we believe in a healthy ecosystem where people can find the tools that work for them.

Stability, and hopefully faster development! Graduating from a side job to a fully maintained and funded project will allow Jun to better guide the contributors and build for the long-term. oMLX stays Apache 2.0, and Jun keeps leading it as before.

Our end goal is to unblock the community to run local AI in any shape or form, and provide the tools and building blocks to make that happen. We expect oMLX to serve as a testbed for new ideas, while leveraging the foundational work of the dependencies it already relies upon, such as mlx-lm or mlx-vlm. We believe that strong modeling and inference libraries help the community, so we'd love to upstream work to wherever it makes sense. We have been collaborating with many projects mlx-lm, mlx-vlm, LMStudio, and we hope we can strengthen the relationship with Cheng, Prince, Yagil, and their teams to better serve the community together.

Concretely, one focus area is the quick transition from a transformers model definition to a reference MLX implementation that can be consumed by different engines, so each one can focus on the unique features they provide. The transformers library has become the reference for ML model definitions, we want to streamline the process to make new transformers models run on MLX.

We are incredibly excited about the future.

financeStories.fullTranslation:
MLX 是苹果公司专为 Apple Silicon 优化的本地 AI 框架。自 2023 年 Awni 和 Angelos 将其作为圣诞礼物发布以来，我们便一直是 MLX 的坚定支持者；我们也很自豪 Hugging Face 能够成为大家寻找 MLX 模型并贡献自身成果的中心枢纽（Hub）。开源、本地 AI 的使用正在加速普及，我们深信一个健康的生态系统应当能让每个人都找到适合自己的工具。

稳定性，以及有望实现更快的开发节奏！从一项业余副业转变为拥有全职维护和资金支持的项目，将让 Jun 能够更好地指导贡献者，并进行长远规划与构建。oMLX 依然保持 Apache 2.0 开源协议，Jun 也将一如既往地继续主导该项目。

我们的终极目标是扫除社区以任何形式运行本地 AI 的阻碍，并提供实现这一目标所需的工具和基础设施构建模块。我们期望 oMLX 能够充当新创意的试验田，同时充分利用其现已依赖的基础工作，例如 mlx-lm 或 mlx-vlm。我们坚信强大的建模与推理库对社区大有裨益，因此只要合理可行，我们非常乐意将工作向上游回馈贡献。我们一直在与 mlx-lm、mlx-vlm、LMStudio 等众多项目开展合作，并且希望能进一步加强与 Cheng、Prince、Yagil 及其团队的联系，共同更好地为社区服务。

具体而言，一个核心重点领域是实现从 transformers 模型定义到可供不同引擎使用的参考 MLX 实现的快速过渡，以便各引擎能够专注于自身提供的独特特性。transformers 库已成为机器学习模型定义的事实标准，我们希望简化这一流程，使新的 transformers 模型能够无缝在 MLX 上运行。

我们对未来充满期待与兴奋。
