See All Transportation

The line has been repaired, but delays are ongoing.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by TC Sottek

Hundreds of flights were cancelled or delayed on Monday after construction crews in New Jersey accidentally cut a Verizon fiber cable used for air traffic control.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said that a circuit failure led to the discovery of the severed fiber cable, ABC News reports. The outage hammered airports across the Northeast, causing ground stops at all three major New York City airports.

In a statement to CNBC, Verizon said that it bore “no responsibility for this incident,” putting the blame on “construction contractors working in the area” that “dug up and cut our cable.”

Ironically, it looks like trains make have taken out the planes, but fingers are still being pointed. US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said an Amtrak crew accidentally cut the line, but AP reports that Amtrak blames a New Jersey Transit crew for the disruption. “This incident occurred on New Jersey Transit property and involved a New Jersey Transit contractor,” an Amtrak spokesperson told NBC4.

As of Monday evening, Duffy said that “the telecom lines have been repaired, and all airport operations in the Northeast are resuming,” but cautioned that it will take “some time to clear all existing delays.” According to FlightAware, there were over 1,000 canceled flights today in the US

aiStories.title: 研究表明：年轻用户（9至18岁）弃用谷歌转向人工智能，后果尚不可知
aiStories.originalTitle: Study: Young users (9 to 18Y) ditch Google for AI, with unknown consequences
aiStories.fullContent:
School researchers reviewed nearly 200 studies on how artificial intelligence affects children and young people’s ability to learn and think. They found that we know very little about how AI use impacts younger school children.

Researchers wanted to find out how AI tools affect students' critical thinking and problem-solving abilities. They analysed 173 international studies that had looked at the use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in school and education.

Storrøsæter has analysed 173 international research articles on the use of generative artificial intelligence (machine learning techniques where the goal is not only to analyse data, but also to create new data, for example in the form of text, images, audio, video or programming code. The most widespread use of generative AI is through chatbots, such as ChatGPT) in school work and education. Her study was conducted with a group of colleagues from Czech universities.

The goal of the literature review was to find out whether AI tools strengthen or weaken children and youths’ ability to think critically and solve problems independently. Many people believe that these skills have never been more important than now, in the 21st century.

“The most important finding is that AI in and of itself does not make us any better or worse at thinking. It’s easy to believe that the tools will either strengthen or weaken learning. We found a clear dual effect. The same technology can do both,” said Storrøsæter, who is also a geographer and teacher who focuses on subject-matter pedagogy.

“The study confirms the dual nature of AI. The same technology can have both constructive and destructive effects. We were surprised that this came across so clearly,” says Hilde Storrøsæter, a PhD research fellow at NTNU’s Department of Teacher Education. Photo: NTNU SHOW MORE

AI tools support important skills when they are used to challenge, ask questions, compare different viewpoints and build one’s own line of reasoning.

“But when AI becomes a shortcut to a ready-made answer, the chance of overdependence, more superficial thinking and weakened independent problem solving increases,” Storrøsæter says.

The Norwegian Media Authority’s survey (in Norwegian) on the media habits of 9 to 18-year-olds shows that the use of Google searches fell from 72% in 2024 to 47% in 2026 for this age group.

The report shows that 39% of Norwegian 11 to 12-year-olds use AI.

The website ung.no – Norway’s online information and communication channel for young people aged 13 to 20 – is also losing traffic because young people are switching to AI tools to find answers to their questions. The number of visits to ung.no fell from 24 million to 18 million from 2024 to 2025. Google’s new AI summaries have also influenced the decline in traffic.

The researchers analysed studies from 2022 – the year that AI language models swept onto the world stage – and up to the spring of 2025. Few predicted the power and speed with which technology would change society. AI affects how information is created, used, shared and disseminated. The consequences are particularly significant in schools and educational settings.

The education sector has already been shaped by AI. The question is whether we can shape the use of AI.

Research on the use of AI in education should provide direction for pedagogy, policy and research in the field to help authorities and other institutions make decisions on AI use.

Storrøsæter and her colleagues uncovered three major gaps in what we know about AI use.

In 80% of the studies the researchers analysed, the participants were university or college students. This means that we know surprisingly little about the academic and cognitive effects of AI use on children and youths, at a time while they are still developing how they perceive, process and evaluate information.

“We can’t simply assume that what applies to a 22-year-old university student also applies to a 10- or 14-year-old,” says Storrøsæter.

“If AI takes over the thinking process before pupils have had time to develop their own skills for critical thinking and problem solving, the consequences could be completely different for them than for adults,” she says.

You might also like: “We must develop thinkers. Not crammers and fact-experts”

Most of the articles in the literature review are based on self-reporting. This is considered a less reliable method than objective studies of changes over time.

The school researchers also uncovered a geographically skewed distribution in where the studies were done. South Asia, Southeast Asia and East Asia – primarily China – dominate with 28 studies. In Europe, Spain and the United Kingdom led with nine studies each.

A total of 15 studies were conducted in the USA. Africa, South America and Central Asia are seriously underrepresented. This creates a research gap that should be addressed.

Overall, the studies show positive effects more often than negative ones.

The researchers behind the new literature review highlight three crucial issues in particular: How AI tools are used, teachers’ understanding of AI, and the demands teachers place on students and pupils.

“Teacher education has a dual task. We have to educate teachers who can use and relate critically to AI themselves. At the same time, our education students should also be able to teach children and young people how to use AI. It is not enough to just teach them to use some AI tools,” says Storrøsæter.

For us to succeed with AI in schools, teacher education has to succeed.

“Students need to understand what technology does to the learning process itself, such as what happens when AI solves parts of the task. Which parts of the thinking process are important for the pupils to still do themselves? How do we design tasks where AI becomes a tool, and not a replacement, for thinking?”

Storrøsæter is not worried about students’ or pupils’ use of AI in and of itself.

“I support being restrictive in terms of not using AI with very young pupils. But when AI is used, it has to happen on the teacher’s terms,” she says.

If AI is used uncritically, you don’t build any skills with it, and you miss out on a lot of learning situations. This will only increase disparities between those who use AI critically and as a tool, and those who use it uncritically simply to complete a task faster. If that happens, schools and universities will both face significant challenges.

Technology will probably continue to develop faster than we can put curricula and regulations in place. Our number one task is therefore to cultivate AI literacy, by protecting and developing competence in critical thinking, problem solving, source criticism and the ability to make independent assessments.

“The education sector is already strongly influenced and shaped by AI. The question is whether we can shape the use of AI so that it supports students’ thinking instead of taking it over.”

Storrøsæter stresses that if we are to succeed with AI in schools, teacher education has to succeed.

Reference: Tomáš Bendl, Lenka Krajňáková, Hilde Storrøsæter, Emil Drápela, Martin Hanus: Dual Nature of GenAI: Catalyst or Barrier for Critical Thinking and Problem-Solving Skills? A systematic Review, Journal of Information Technology Education: Research • Volume 25 • 2026 • https://doi.org/10.28945/5834

教育学者回顾了近200项关于人工智能如何影响儿童和青少年学习与思考能力的研究。他们发现，对于人工智能的使用究竟如何影响低龄学童，我们知之甚少。

研究人员希望了解人工智能工具如何影响学生的批判性思维与解决问题的能力。他们分析了173项探讨生成式人工智能（GenAI）在学校和教育中应用的国际研究。

斯托罗塞特（Storrøsæter）分析了173篇关于生成式人工智能（一种机器学习技术，其目标不仅是分析数据，还包括生成新数据，例如文本、图像、音频、视频或编程代码形式；生成式人工智能最广泛的应用形式是聊天机器人，例如ChatGPT）在学业和教育中应用的国际研究论文。她的这项研究是与来自捷克多所大学的同事共同开展的。

这项文献综述的目标，是探究人工智能工具究竟会增强还是削弱儿童和青少年批判性思考以及独立解决问题的能力。许多人认为，在21世纪的当下，这些技能比以往任何时候都更加重要。

“最重要的发现是，人工智能本身并不会让我们在思考上变得更好或更差。人们很容易认为这些工具要么增强学习，要么削弱学习。但我们发现了一种明显的双重效应。同一项技术可能产生这两种完全不同的效果，”斯托罗塞特说道，她同时也是一名专注于学科教学法的地理学者与教师。

“这项研究证实了人工智能的双重特性。同一项技术既能产生建设性效果，也能产生破坏性影响。这种现象表现得如此鲜明，让我们感到惊讶，”挪威科技大学（NTNU）教师教育系博士后研究员希尔德·斯托罗塞特（Hilde Storrøsæter）表示。图片来源：NTNU 展开更多

当人工智能工具被用于提出挑战、发起质疑、对比不同观点以及构建个人论证逻辑时，它们能够对重要技能提供支持。

“但当人工智能变成获取现成答案的捷径时，过度依赖、思维浅层化以及独立解决问题能力削弱的风险就会上升，”斯托罗塞特表示。

挪威媒体管理局针对9至18岁人群媒体习惯的调查显示，在这一年龄段中，使用谷歌搜索的比例从2024年的72%骤降至2026年的47%。

该报告显示，39%的挪威11至12岁儿童使用人工智能。

面向13至20岁青少年的挪威在线信息与沟通渠道——网站 ung.no，其访问量也出现了下滑，原因是年轻人正在转向人工智能工具来寻找问题答案。ung.no的访问量从2024年的2400万次下滑至2025年的1800万次。谷歌最新推出的人工智能摘要功能同样对流量的下滑产生了影响。

研究人员分析了从2022年（人工智能语言模型席卷全球舞台的年份）至2025年春季的研究。很少有人预料到这项技术改变社会的力量与速度。人工智能影响了信息的创建、使用、共享和传播方式。这种后果在学校和教育环境中尤为显著。

教育领域已经被人工智能所重塑。核心问题在于我们是否能够引导和塑造人工智能的使用。

关于人工智能在教育中应用的研究应当为该领域的教学法、政策与学术研究指明方向，以帮助主管当局和其他机构就人工智能的使用做出决策。

斯托罗塞特及其同事揭示了当前我们对人工智能使用认知的三个主要空白。

在研究人员分析的文献中，80%的研究对象为大学或学院学生。这意味着，当儿童和青少年仍在发展他们感知、处理和评估信息的能力时，我们对人工智能使用带给他们的学业与认知影响知之甚少，令人惊讶。

“我们不能简单地假定适用于22岁大学生的结论同样适用于10岁或14岁的孩子，”斯托罗塞特表示。

“如果人工智能在学生尚未来得及培养出自己的批判性思维和解决问题能力之前就接管了思考过程，那么对其产生的后果可能与对成年人完全不同，”她说道。

您可能还喜欢：“我们必须培养思考者，而不是死记硬背者和事实专家”

文献综述中的大部分文章均基于自我报告数据。相比于跨时间变化的长周期客观研究，这种方法被认为可靠性较低。

教育学者们还揭示了研究开展地域分布上的不均衡。南亚、东南亚和东亚（主要是中国）以28项研究占据主导。在欧洲，西班牙和英国各以9项研究领先。

在美国共开展了15项研究。非洲、南美洲和中亚地区的代表性严重不足。这就造成了一个亟待填补的研究空白。

总体而言，研究显示的积极影响多于消极影响。

新文献综述背后的研究人员特别强调了三个关键议题：人工智能工具的具体使用方式、教师对人工智能的理解，以及教师对中小学生提出的要求。

“教师教育肩负着双重任务。我们必须培养出自身能够使用并批判性对待人工智能的教师。与此同时，我们的师范生还应当有能力教会儿童和青少年如何使用人工智能。仅仅教他们使用某些人工智能工具是远远不够的，”斯托罗塞特表示。

为了使人工智能在学校教育中取得成功，教师教育必须首先取得成功。

“学生需要理解这项技术对学习过程本身造成了什么影响，例如当人工智能解决了一部分任务时会发生什么。思考过程中的哪些部分是仍然必须由学生自己完成的关键环节？我们该如何设计作业任务，使人工智能成为思考的工具，而不是替代思考的工具？”

斯托罗塞特本身并不担心学生使用人工智能这件事本身。

“我支持对极低龄学童采取限制使用人工智能的做法。但当人工智能被使用时，必须在教师设定的规则与要求下进行，”她表示。

如果缺乏批判性地使用人工智能，你无法凭借它构建任何技能，而且会错失大量的学习情境。这只会加剧两极分化：一边是批判性地将人工智能作为工具使用的人，另一边则是为了更快完成任务而盲目使用的人。若这种情况发生，学校和大学都将面临巨大挑战。

技术的演进速度可能仍将快于我们制定课程体系和监管政策的速度。因此，我们的首要任务是培养人工智能素养，通过保护和发展批判性思维、解决问题、信源甄别以及做出独立评估的能力来筑牢根基。

“教育领域已经深受人工智能的影响与塑造。现在的关键在于，我们是否能够引导和塑造人工智能的使用，使其支持而不是取代学生的思考。”

斯托罗塞特（Storrøsæter）强调，如果我们想在学校成功推广人工智能，教师教育必须率先取得成功。

参考文献：Tomáš Bendl, Lenka Krajňáková, Hilde Storrøsæter, Emil Drápela, Martin Hanus: 《生成式人工智能的双重属性：批判性思维与解决问题能力的催化剂还是绊脚石？系统性文献综述》（Dual Nature of GenAI: Catalyst or Barrier for Critical Thinking and Problem-Solving Skills? A systematic Review），载于《信息技术教育研究杂志》（Journal of Information Technology Education: Research）• 第25卷 • 2026年 • https://doi.org/10.28945/5834

aiStories.title: 苹果首个现场音乐场馆即将于其英国总部地下落成开放
aiStories.originalTitle: Apple’s first live music venue is opening beneath its UK headquarters
aiStories.snippet: The venue is opening below Battersea Power Station, also well recognized for featuring on the cover of Pink Floyd’s Animals album. | Image: Apple Apple is preparing to open a new "state-of-the-art" live music venue in the UK, a 600-capacity space for hosting performances, recording sessions, and video broadcasts. The venue, called Apple Music Hall, is located underneath Apple's European headquarters in London's iconic Battersea Power Station, and is set to open next week on September 28th. Detai
aiStories.fullContent: Apple is preparing to open a new “state-of-the-art” live music venue in the UK, a 600-capacity space for hosting performances, recording sessions, and video broadcasts. The venue, called Apple Music Hall, is located underneath Apple’s European headquarters in London’s iconic Battersea Power Station, and is set to open next week on September 28th. Details about the opening show have yet to be announced. “Apple’s deep love for music dates all the way back to the very beginning, from the launch of the iPod to the long-running iTunes Music Festival to the debut of Apple Music,” said Oliver Schusser, Apple’s vice president of Apple Music and International Content. “Today, with the opening of Apple Music Hall, we are once again taking an unprecedented step further in our commitment to artists and fans by supporting live music in ways only Apple can do.” [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Hall-event-space-01.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Hall-event-space-02.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Hall-foyer-angle-02.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] The limited capacity and layout is “designed intentionally to close the gap between intimacy and production value,” according to Apple’s announcement, with seating that feels close to the performer while providing artists with a 38-foot-wide stage that can be reconfigured to their needs. Apple Music Hall has a 48-speaker spatial sound system positioned around the audience, is hardwired for 16 or more broadcast cameras, and includes two dedicated recording and mixing studios behind the stage that allow it to operate as a full production facility. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Radio-greenroom.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Radio-VIP-greenroom.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Radio-A-list-corridor.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Radio-greenroom-hair-makeup.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] The performance space is opening alongside new Apple Music radio studios in Battersea, with Apple announcing that all of its London-based hosts and shows will now broadcast from the facility. “We’re always looking for new opportunities to connect the artists and the fans because we are fans,” said Apple Music’s global creative director, Zane Lowe. “Great music and memories will be made at Apple Music Hall.” [Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_srDnNd9iaE] Apple Music Hall marks the company’s return to London’s music scene, having previously run the iTunes Music Festival in England’s capital city for a decade — hosting acts like One Direction, Lady Gaga, Elton John, and Adele at intimate local venues — before its cancellation in 2017. Battersea Power Station, a decommissioned Art Deco facility that reopened in 2022, also has its own roots in music history, having appeared on the cover of Pink Floyd’s Animals album.

苹果公司正准备在英国开设一个全新的“尖端”现场音乐场馆。这是一个可容纳600人的空间，用于举办演出、录音以及视频转播。该场馆名为“Apple Music Hall”，位于苹果欧洲总部所在地——伦敦标志性建筑巴特西发电站（Battersea Power Station）的地下，定于下周9月28日正式开放。首场演出的详细信息尚未公布。

苹果公司负责 Apple Music 及国际内容业务的副总裁奥利弗·舒塞尔（Oliver Schusser）表示：“苹果对音乐的热爱可一路追溯到最开端，从 iPod 的推出，到长期举办的 iTunes 音乐节，再到 Apple Music 的亮相。今天，随着 Apple Music Hall 的开幕，我们再次迈出了前所未有的一步，以只有苹果才能做到的方式支持现场音乐，践行我们对艺术家和乐迷的承诺。”

[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Hall-event-space-01.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Hall-event-space-02.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Hall-foyer-angle-02.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

据苹果官方公告，有限的容纳人数和场地布局是“特意为了拉近亲近感与制作水准之间的距离而设计”。观众席让人感觉与表演者近在咫尺，同时为艺术家提供了一个38英尺宽、可根据其需求重新布局的舞台。Apple Music Hall 围绕观众配备了由48个扬声器组成的空间音频系统，预先布线支持16台或更多转播摄像机，并在后台设有两个专门的录音和混音工作室，使其能够作为一个功能齐全的制作中心运转。

[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Radio-greenroom.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Radio-VIP-greenroom.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Radio-A-list-corridor.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-Music-Radio-greenroom-hair-makeup.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

该演出空间与巴特西的新 Apple Music 电台演播室一同启用。苹果宣布，其常驻伦敦的所有主持人及节目今后都将从该设施进行播出。“我们一直在寻找新的机会来连接艺术家和歌迷，因为我们自己也是乐迷，”Apple Music 全球创意总监赞恩·洛（Zane Lowe）说，“伟大的音乐和回忆将在 Apple Music Hall 诞生。”

[Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_srDnNd9iaE]

Apple Music Hall 标志着该公司重返伦敦音乐界。此前，苹果曾在这座英国首都举办过长达十年的 iTunes 音乐节——在当地亲密的小型场馆中邀请了单向组合（One Direction）、Lady Gaga、埃尔顿·约翰（Elton John）和阿黛尔（Adele）等知名艺人表演，该音乐节于2017年停办。巴特西发电站是一处停运的装饰艺术风格工业建筑，于2022年重新开放，它在音乐史上也拥有深厚渊源，曾登上平克·弗洛伊德（Pink Floyd）乐队《Animals》专辑的封面。

aiStories.title: gzip 能充当语言模型吗？
aiStories.originalTitle: Can gzip be a language model?
aiStories.fullContent:
A while back I wrote about language modeling without neural networks, where I generated Shakespeare with an unbounded n-gram model: no weights, no training, just counting. Fortuitously, I came across the paper Language Modeling is Compression, which mentioned the compression–prediction equivalence:

every prediction model is inherently a compressor, and all compression algorithms are prediction models.

This led to the natural question: can gzip do language modeling?1 No neural network, no learned parameters, nothing. Just the compressor that ships with your operating system. You prime it with a corpus, give it a normal text prompt, and it continues that prompt by searching for the byte sequences that compress best. Here’s some real, unedited output after priming it on tiny Shakespeare:

It turns out, kind of? It’s not exactly coherent text, but it clearly knows something about the text. Much more than I expected gzip to know.2 So how can a compressor generate this?

Think about what a compressor does. It spends few bytes on data it “expects” and many bytes on data it doesn’t. If I hand you a file that’s the letter A repeated a million times, you can describe it in one sentence. A million random bytes, on the other hand, have no structure to exploit and barely compress at all.

This is not a coincidence; it’s the core of information theory. The number of bits needed to encode a symbol is $-\log_2 p$, where $p$ is the probability the model assigns to it. High probability means few bits. So any compressor has a probability model hiding inside it, whether or not anyone wrote one down.

gzip uses DEFLATE, which compresses the next bytes by finding matches against the recent text in a 32 KiB sliding window. If a continuation echoes something already in the window, DEFLATE encodes it as a cheap back-reference instead of literal bytes. So:

A continuation that gzip “expected”, because it echoes text already in its window, compresses to almost nothing.

That gives us a score. If I have some context and I want to know how good a candidate continuation is, I just measure:

The smaller the compressed length, the more “predicted” the candidate is. To prime the model, I include a corpus in gzip’s window. Any continuation that looks like the corpus compresses small, and any continuation that doesn’t compresses large.

Scoring is one thing; generating is another. The naive approach of picking the single next byte that compresses best fails badly, and for a subtle reason: gzip only gives an integer byte length (no fractions). Adding one byte often doesn’t change the compressed length at all, so many candidates tie and the signal is buried in quantization noise.

The fix is to look ahead a whole span before committing. gzipt runs a beam search over byte sequences. At each step, the current context is:

Then gzipt tries possible next bytes. Each candidate continuation is scored by compressing context + candidate and checking how many bytes the compressed result takes.

One detail that matters is that only the last tail bytes of generated output stay in the scoring context. DEFLATE codes nearby matches more cheaply than far ones, so if gzip could see its entire history, the cheapest thing to do is often to fall into verbatim loops, repeatedly copying text it just emitted.

You can see the decoding and scoring process in the animation above, which is the same replay shown at the top. The whole thing is one file of pure standard-library Python (just zlib). Code’s on GitHub if you want to play with it.

The paper did try this, but it ended up performing poorly. Adding beam search significantly improved generation quality (an idea they mentioned), which is discussed below. ↩︎

The code actually uses zlib instead of spawning a gzip process, but the name GziPT was too good. I believe they both use the same DEFLATE algorithm under the hood. ↩︎
aiStories.fullTranslation:
前段时间我写过一篇关于无需神经网络进行语言建模的文章，当时我用一个无界 n-gram 模型生成了莎士比亚风格的文本：没有权重，没有训练，仅仅是计数。机缘巧合下，我看到了论文《语言建模即压缩》（Language Modeling is Compression），其中提到了压缩与预测的等价性：
每一个预测模型本质上都是一个压缩器，而所有压缩算法也都是预测模型。
这引出了一个很自然的问题：gzip 能用来做语言建模吗？¹ 不需要神经网络，没有学习得到的参数，什么都没有。就用你操作系统自带的压缩工具。你先用一个语料库对其进行预热（prime），给它一个常规的文本提示词，然后它通过搜索压缩效果最好的字节序列来续写该提示词。以下是在用微型莎士比亚（tiny Shakespeare）语料库预热后，生成的真实且未经编辑的输出：
结果表明，似乎还真行？虽然它算不上完全连贯的文本，但显然对文本是有所了解的。这远远超出了我对 gzip 认知能力的预期。² 那么，压缩器究竟是如何生成这些内容的呢？
不妨想一想压缩器在做什么。对于它“预期中”的数据，它只需花费很少的字节；而对于它“未曾预期”的数据，则要消耗很多字节。如果我递给你一个重复了一百万次字母 A 的文件，你用一句话就能描述它。相反，一百万个随机字节则没有任何可利用的结构，几乎完全无法压缩。
这绝非巧合，而是信息论的核心所在。对一个符号进行编码所需的比特数为 $-\log_2 p$，其中 $p$ 是模型赋予它的概率。概率越高意味着所需的比特数越少。因此，任何压缩器内部都隐藏着一个概率模型，无论是否有人显式写出过它。
gzip 采用的是 DEFLATE 算法，它通过在 32 KiB 的滑动窗口中查找与近期文本匹配的内容来压缩后续字节。如果续写内容呼应了窗口中已有的内容，DEFLATE 就会将其编码为低开销的后向引用，而不是原样输出字面量字节。因此：
一个 gzip “预期中”的续写——因为它呼应了其窗口中已有的文本——几乎可以被压缩至忽略不计。
这就为我们提供了一个评分标准。如果我有一些上下文，想要知道某个候选续写有多好，我只需要测量：
压缩后的长度越小，说明该候选续写被“预测”的程度越高。为了预热模型，我将一个语料库放入 gzip 的窗口中。任何看起来像该语料库的续写内容，压缩后体积都很小；而任何不像它的内容，压缩后体积都很大。
评分是一回事，生成则是另一回事。直接选取压缩效果最好的下一个字节这种朴素方法彻底失败了，原因很微妙：gzip 只给出整数形式的字节长度（没有小数分值）。添加一个字节往往根本不会改变压缩后的长度，因此许多候选续写会打成平手，有效信号被淹没在量化噪声中。
解决办法是在最终确定前向前看完整的一个跨度（span）。gzipt 对字节序列执行束搜索（beam search）。在每一步中，当前的上下文为：
接着 gzipt 会尝试可能的下一个字节。通过压缩“上下文 + 候选续写”并检查压缩结果占用多少字节，来对每个候选续写进行评分。
一个关键细节是：生成的输出中只有最后的末尾字节会保留在评分上下文中。DEFLATE 对临近匹配的编码开销比远距离匹配更低，因此如果 gzip 能看到它的全部历史，开销最小的做法往往是陷入逐字死循环，不断重复复制它刚刚吐出的文本。
你可以在上面的动画中看到解码和评分过程，这与顶部展示的回放相同。整个实现是一个纯标准库的 Python 文件（仅使用了 zlib）。如果你想尝试一下，代码已开源在 GitHub 上。
论文中确实尝试过这种方法，但最终表现较差。加入束搜索显著提升了生成质量（这是他们提到过的一个想法），下文对此进行了讨论。↩︎
代码实际上使用的是 zlib 而不是直接调用 gzip 进程，但 GziPT 这个名字实在太贴切了。我相信它们底层使用的都是相同的 DEFLATE 算法。↩︎

aiStories.title: Morphotonics 筹集 4000 万欧元，将其显示技术扩展至数据中心领域
aiStories.originalTitle: Morphotonics raises €40M to expand its display tech into data centers
aiStories.snippet: Deeptech company Morphotonics raises €40M from investors including 3M Ventures, Innovation Industries, BOM, and Invest-NL.
aiStories.fullContent:
The Netherlands’ ASML is possibly the biggest name in lithography, using its machines to etch patterns onto silicon wafers inside a computer chip factory known as a fab. Fellow Dutch company Morphotonics is smaller and works in a different corner of the same field: nanoimprint lithography, or NIL, a process used to manufacture the displays in AR glasses and other optics. It said it has benefited from ASML’s supply chain and uses many of the same vendors.

Morphotonics has spent 12 years developing that technology, largely under the radar. Now, as demand for smart glasses and other optics surges, the company said Tuesday it has raised €40 million to scale up production and push into a new market: optical components for data centers.The round was backed by 3M Ventures, Innovation Industries, BOM, and Invest-NL. The European Innovation Council (EIC) Fund; Ernij Next, a Dutch family office; and the European Investment Bank (EIB) also participated.

Morphotonics’ NIL work means the startup creates a “stamp” and applies it to photosensitive materials to create various kinds of displays, from augmented reality glasses to privacy screens for cars.

This is useful in creating the waveguide technology used in smart glasses, including the Meta Ray-Ban Display, Even Reality, and Magic Leap. Waveguides are thin pieces of glass or plastic that deflect light along a specific path so that they display an image in front of the wearer’s eyes.

Smart glasses are just one application of Morphotonics’ technology, but it’s currently the most in-demand one. This week, China said sales of smart glasses in the country doubled in the first eight months of this year. In June, the market research firm IDC noted that shipments of smart glasses with displays are expected to reach 12.2 million by 2030. As that market grows, manufacturers are looking for machines like Morphotonics’ that can produce those displays at scale.

The latest fundraising is part of an extended round that began in 2024, raised in multiple installments. The company has used the money to more than double its headcount to 60 employees, up from roughly 30 in September 2024, when CEO Hugo Da Silva joined. Morphotonics still plans to hire and expects headcount to stabilize around 70 to 75 people.

“Typically, display manufacturers would acquire our equipment as part of the supply chain, and we integrate it into the entire manufacturing process. We teach them the process, we provide the chemicals, and they can manufacture that,” Da Silva said. The company’s manufacturing is heavily concentrated in Asia, with teams in China, Taiwan, South Korea, and the U.S. “Strong local presence is very important,” he said.

Da Silva said the company’s next machine, currently being built, will be capable of producing more than 6 million waveguides a year. He said it’s expected to start shipping early next year.

Beyond displays, that expansion also includes a push into co-packaged optics, a technology used in data centers that use Photonic Integrated Circuits — chips that use light instead of electricity — to move data between servers and network equipment. The startup hasn’t shipped any machines in this area, but it said customers have validated its tech.

The company sells both hardware machines and the process through licensing to ensure that customers get the best results. Right now, roughly 90% of the startup’s revenue comes from hardware sales, with 10 to 15 systems deployed globally. The company expects to reach 50 deployments in the next two to three years, which should also increase its revenue from services.

aiStories.fullTranslation:
荷兰的阿斯麦（ASML）可能是光刻领域最负盛名的企业，其机器被用于在被称为晶圆厂的计算机芯片工厂内将图案蚀刻到硅晶圆上。同为荷兰公司的 Morphotonics 规模相对较小，并在同一领域的另一个细分方向深耕：纳米压印光刻（nanoimprint lithography，简称 NIL），一种用于制造 AR 眼镜及其他光学器件中显示屏的工艺。该公司表示，自身受益于 ASML 的供应链，并且采用了许多相同的供应商。

Morphotonics 花了 12 年时间研发这项技术，在此期间大部分时间都鲜为人知。如今，随着对智能眼镜及其他光学器件的需求激增，该公司周二宣布已筹集 4000 万欧元，用于扩大生产规模并进军一个新市场：数据中心光学组件。本轮融资由 3M Ventures、Innovation Industries、BOM 和 Invest-NL 领投/参投。欧洲创新理事会（EIC）基金、荷兰家族办公室 Ernij Next 以及欧洲投资银行（EIB）也参与了投资。

Morphotonics 的 NIL 业务意味着该初创公司会制作一个“压印模具”，并将其压印于光敏材料上，从而制造各种显示产品，从增强现实眼镜到汽车防窥屏皆涵盖其中。

这对于制造智能眼镜（包括 Meta Ray-Ban Display、Even Reality 和 Magic Leap）所使用的光波导技术非常有用。光波导是轻薄的玻璃或塑料片，能将光线沿特定路径偏转，从而在佩戴者眼前呈现图像。

智能眼镜只是 Morphotonics 技术的应用场景之一，但目前是需求最为迫切的场景。本周，中国方面表示，今年前八个月该国智能眼镜销量翻了一番。今年 6 月，市场研究机构 IDC 指出，到 2030 年，带显示屏的智能眼镜出货量预计将达到 1220 万台。随着这一市场的增长，制造商正在寻找像 Morphotonics 这样能够大规模生产此类显示屏的设备。

最新的这一轮融资始于 2024 年，是一轮分多期筹集的扩展轮融资。公司已利用这笔资金将员工人数增加了一倍多，达到 60 人，而在 2024 年 9 月现任首席执行官雨果·达席尔瓦（Hugo Da Silva）加入时大约只有 30 人。Morphotonics 仍计划继续扩招，预计员工人数将稳定在 70 至 75 人左右。

“通常情况下，显示器制造商会将我们的设备作为其供应链的一部分进行采购，我们则将其集成到整个制造流程中。我们向他们传授工艺，提供化学试剂，他们便可进行生产，”达席尔瓦说。该公司的制造业务高度集中在亚洲，并在中国大陆、中国台湾、韩国和美国设有团队。“拥有强大的本土业务网络非常重要，”他表示。

达席尔瓦透露，公司目前正在制造的下一代设备每年将能够生产超过 600 万套光波导。他表示，预计该设备将于明年初开始出货。

除显示器件外，此次业务扩张还包括进军共封装光学（CPO）领域，这是数据中心中使用的一种技术，通过光子集成电路（PIC，即用光代替电来传输数据的芯片）在服务器与网络设备之间传输数据。这家初创公司尚未在该领域交付任何设备，但表示客户已经验证了其技术。

该公司既销售硬件设备，也通过技术授权提供工艺服务，以确保客户获得最佳效果。目前，该公司约 90% 的收入来自硬件销售，全球已部署了 10 到 15 套系统。该公司预计在未来两到三年内将部署量增加至 50 套，这也将提高其服务收入。

aiStories.originalTitle: MiMo-v2.6-Pro: Intelligence, Performance and Price Analysis
aiStories.fullContent:
Released September 2026

MiMo-V2.6-Pro is amongst the leading models in intelligence and reasonably priced when comparing to other open weight models of similar size. It's also notably fast, however somewhat verbose. The model supports text, image, speech, and video input, outputs text, and has a 1M tokens context window.

MiMo-V2.6-Pro scores 46 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, placing it well above average among comparable models (median: 18). When evaluating the Intelligence Index, it generated 140M tokens, which is somewhat verbose in comparison to the median of 140M.

Pricing for MiMo-V2.6-Pro is $0.43 per 1M input tokens (somewhat expensive, median: $0.30) and $0.87 per 1M output tokens (moderately priced, median: $1.13). In total, it cost $206.66 to evaluate MiMo-V2.6-Pro on the Intelligence Index.

At 125 tokens per second, MiMo-V2.6-Pro is notably fast (75).

This page shows the reasoning version of this model.

A non-reasoning variant may also exist.

Supports: text, image, speech, and video

Metrics are compared against models of the same class:

Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2 includes: AA-Briefcase v1.1, GDPval-AA v2.1, AutomationBench-AA, Terminal-Bench 4.0, SciCode, Humanity's Last Exam, GDP.pdf, CritPt, AA-Omniscience, AA-LCR v1.1. See Intelligence Index methodology for further details, including a breakdown of each evaluation and how we run them.

Indicates whether the model weights are available. Models are labelled as 'Commercial Use Restricted' if commercial use is limited by conditions, and as 'Non-commercial' if the license prohibits commercial use.

Measures the performance of models on specific capabilities and industries

Agentic knowledge work, (Elo-500)/2000

Quantitative analysis on spreadsheets & documents

Kubernetes incident root-cause analysis

Medical long context reasoning

While model intelligence generally translates across use cases, specific evaluations may be more relevant for certain use cases.

AA-Briefcase Elo is a combined metric that aggregates analytical quality Elo, presentation Elo, and rubric pass rate, with rubric performance converted into Elo via synthetic head-to-head matches. Elo and 95% confidence interval bounds are clamped at 0.

AA-Omniscience Index (higher is better) measures knowledge reliability and hallucination. It rewards correct answers, penalizes hallucinations, and has no penalty for refusing to answer. Scores range from -100 to 100, where 0 means as many correct as incorrect answers, and negative scores mean more incorrect than correct.

Weighted average cost per Intelligence Index task. Each evaluation’s cost is calculated from input, cache hit, cache write, reasoning, and answer token prices, divided by task count, and weighted by its Intelligence Index weight.

The number of tokens required per Intelligence Index task. This is calculated by multiplying the output tokens per eval by the relative weights of each benchmark in the Intelligence Index, then dividing by task count (excluding repeats).

The cost to run the evaluations in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, calculated using the model's input, cache hit, cache write, reasoning, and answer token prices and the number of tokens used across evaluations (excluding repeats).

Price per token for cached prompts (previously processed), typically offering a significant discount compared to regular input price, represented as USD per million tokens. The values shown here are the cache hit price; cache write and cache storage are billed separately and vary by provider — see "Cache pricing by provider" for detail.

Larger context windows are relevant to RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) LLM workflows which typically involve reasoning and information retrieval of large amounts of data.

Maximum number of combined input & output tokens. Output tokens commonly have a significantly lower limit (varied by model).

Measured by Output Speed (tokens per second)

Tokens per second received while the model is generating tokens (ie. after first chunk has been received from the API for models which support streaming).

Figures represent performance of the model's first-party API or the median across providers where a first-party API is not available.

The weighted average time (seconds) per Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index task. This is calculated by dividing output tokens per task by output speed, weighted by the relative weights of each benchmark in the Intelligence Index.

Measured by Time (seconds) to First Token

Time to first answer token received, in seconds, after API request sent. For reasoning models, this includes the 'thinking' time of the model before providing an answer. For models which do not support streaming, this represents time to receive the completion.

Seconds to output 500 tokens, calculated based on time to first token, 'thinking' time for reasoning models, and output speed

Seconds to receive a 500 token response. Key components:

The total number of trainable weights and biases in the model, expressed in billions. These parameters are learned during training and determine the model's ability to process and generate responses.

The number of parameters actually executed during each inference forward pass, expressed in billions. For Mixture of Experts (MoE) models, a routing mechanism selects a subset of experts per token, resulting in fewer active than total parameters. Dense models use all parameters, so active equals total.

Common questions about MiMo-V2.6-Pro

MiMo-V2.6-Pro was created by Xiaomi.

MiMo-V2.6-Pro has a time to first token (TTFT) of 2.34s (based on Xiaomi's API), which is better than average compared to other open weight models of similar size (median: 2.33s).

MiMo-V2.6-Pro costs $0.43 per 1M input tokens (better than average, median: $0.45) and $0.87 per 1M output tokens (very competitive, median: $1.68), based on Xiaomi's API.

MiMo-V2.6-Pro costs $0.43 per 1M input tokens and $0.87 per 1M output tokens (based on Xiaomi's API). For a blended rate (7:2:1 cache hit/input/output ratio), this is $0.18 per 1M tokens. Pricing may vary by provider. Compare provider pricing

When evaluated on the Intelligence Index, MiMo-V2.6-Pro generated 140M output tokens, which is somewhat higher than average compared to other open weight models of similar size (median: 140M).

Yes, MiMo-V2.6-Pro is a reasoning model. It uses extended thinking or chain-of-thought reasoning to work through complex problems before providing an answer.

MiMo-V2.6-Pro has a context window of 1.0M tokens. This determines how much text and conversation history the model can process in a single request.

MiMo-V2.6-Pro has 1.0 trillion parameters (42 billion active).

MiMo-V2.6-Pro is a Mixture of Experts (MoE) model with 1.0 trillion total parameters, but only 42 billion active parameters are used during inference.

MiMo-V2.6-Pro is released under the MIT license. This license allows commercial use.

aiStories.title: oMLX 创作者兼维护者 Jun Kim 加入 Hugging Face，助力 MLX 社区发展
aiStories.originalTitle: Jun Kim, oMLX creator and maintainer, joins Hugging Face to support the MLX community
aiStories.fullContent:
MLX is Apple's framework for local AI, especially optimized for Apple Silicon. We are big MLX supporters since it was the Christmas present from Awni and Angelos in 2023, and proud that Hugging Face is the Hub where people find MLX models and contribute their own. Usage of open, local AI is accelerating, and we believe in a healthy ecosystem where people can find the tools that work for them.

Stability, and hopefully faster development! Graduating from a side job to a fully maintained and funded project will allow Jun to better guide the contributors and build for the long-term. oMLX stays Apache 2.0, and Jun keeps leading it as before.

Our end goal is to unblock the community to run local AI in any shape or form, and provide the tools and building blocks to make that happen. We expect oMLX to serve as a testbed for new ideas, while leveraging the foundational work of the dependencies it already relies upon, such as mlx-lm or mlx-vlm. We believe that strong modeling and inference libraries help the community, so we'd love to upstream work to wherever it makes sense. We have been collaborating with many projects mlx-lm, mlx-vlm, LMStudio, and we hope we can strengthen the relationship with Cheng, Prince, Yagil, and their teams to better serve the community together.

Concretely, one focus area is the quick transition from a transformers model definition to a reference MLX implementation that can be consumed by different engines, so each one can focus on the unique features they provide. The transformers library has become the reference for ML model definitions, we want to streamline the process to make new transformers models run on MLX.

We are incredibly excited about the future.

aiStories.fullTranslation:
MLX 是苹果公司专为 Apple Silicon 优化的本地 AI 框架。自 2023 年 Awni 和 Angelos 将其作为圣诞礼物发布以来，我们便一直是 MLX 的坚定支持者；我们也很自豪 Hugging Face 能够成为大家寻找 MLX 模型并贡献自身成果的中心枢纽（Hub）。开源、本地 AI 的使用正在加速普及，我们深信一个健康的生态系统应当能让每个人都找到适合自己的工具。

稳定性，以及有望实现更快的开发节奏！从一项业余副业转变为拥有全职维护和资金支持的项目，将让 Jun 能够更好地指导贡献者，并进行长远规划与构建。oMLX 依然保持 Apache 2.0 开源协议，Jun 也将一如既往地继续主导该项目。

我们的终极目标是扫除社区以任何形式运行本地 AI 的阻碍，并提供实现这一目标所需的工具和基础设施构建模块。我们期望 oMLX 能够充当新创意的试验田，同时充分利用其现已依赖的基础工作，例如 mlx-lm 或 mlx-vlm。我们坚信强大的建模与推理库对社区大有裨益，因此只要合理可行，我们非常乐意将工作向上游回馈贡献。我们一直在与 mlx-lm、mlx-vlm、LMStudio 等众多项目开展合作，并且希望能进一步加强与 Cheng、Prince、Yagil 及其团队的联系，共同更好地为社区服务。

具体而言，一个核心重点领域是实现从 transformers 模型定义到可供不同引擎使用的参考 MLX 实现的快速过渡，以便各引擎能够专注于自身提供的独特特性。transformers 库已成为机器学习模型定义的事实标准，我们希望简化这一流程，使新的 transformers 模型能够无缝在 MLX 上运行。

我们对未来充满期待与兴奋。

The line has been repaired, but delays are ongoing.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by TC Sottek

Hundreds of flights were cancelled or delayed on Monday after construction crews in New Jersey accidentally cut a Verizon fiber cable used for air traffic control.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said that a circuit failure led to the discovery of the severed fiber cable, ABC News reports. The outage hammered airports across the Northeast, causing ground stops at all three major New York City airports.

In a statement to CNBC, Verizon said that it bore “no responsibility for this incident,” putting the blame on “construction contractors working in the area” that “dug up and cut our cable.”

Ironically, it looks like trains make have taken out the planes, but fingers are still being pointed. US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said an Amtrak crew accidentally cut the line, but AP reports that Amtrak blames a New Jersey Transit crew for the disruption. “This incident occurred on New Jersey Transit property and involved a New Jersey Transit contractor,” an Amtrak spokesperson told NBC4.

As of Monday evening, Duffy said that “the telecom lines have been repaired, and all airport operations in the Northeast are resuming,” but cautioned that it will take “some time to clear all existing delays.” According to FlightAware, there were over 1,000 canceled flights today in the US

在给美国消费者新闻与商业频道（CNBC）的一份声明中，威瑞森表示其“对此事件不承担任何责任”，并将责任归咎于“在相关区域作业的施工承包商”，称是他们“挖掘并切断了我们的电缆”。
具有讽刺意味的是，情况看起来像是火车干扰了飞机，但责任究竟在谁仍在相互推诿。美国交通部长肖恩·达菲（Sean Duffy）表示，美铁（Amtrak）的一支施工队意外切断了该线路，但美联社（AP）报道称，美铁将此次中断归咎于新泽西公交公司（New Jersey Transit）的人员。“该事件发生在新泽西公交公司的管辖物业上，涉及新泽西公交公司的一家承包商，”美铁发言人向 NBC4 表示。

aiStories.title: 一手打造苹果零售店的掌门人，并不买账硅谷对AI购物的押注
aiStories.originalTitle: The man who built Apple’s stores doesn’t buy Silicon Valley’s bet on AI shopping
aiStories.snippet: Apple Store architect Ron Johnson says Apple's secret sauce has always been its people.
aiStories.fullContent:
While Silicon Valley is spending billions to make AI agents shop for us, the man who pioneered Apple’s retail stores thinks the industry is overestimating how much of shopping people will hand over to machines — and believes physical stores will continue to thrive.

Ron Johnson, 66, has heard predictions about the demise of physical retail before. He joined Apple in 2000 to build its retail business as online shopping was beginning to take off, and went on to help create a store network that became central to how Apple sells its products and connects with customers.

“AI is a new technology that will improve the online shopping experience,” Johnson said in an interview. “But I don’t know that it’s going to change which way we shop.”

Johnson’s view comes as some of the world’s biggest tech companies are trying to push AI deeper into shopping, betting that agents can automate more of how we find and buy items — a concept commonly called agentic commerce. Google is making that push with its Universal Commerce Protocol, a standard designed to help AI agents take consumers from product discovery to checkout. OpenAI, meanwhile, is turning ChatGPT into a shopping destination where users can research, compare, and, in some cases, even buy products without leaving the chatbot.

Asked whether he could imagine someone letting an agent choose and buy a $1,000 or $2,000 laptop without ever visiting a website or store, Johnson was unequivocal: “Honestly, nobody’s going to do that.”

Buying a laptop, he argued, is too personal a purchase to simply delegate to an AI agent. Buyers want to feel its weight, see the display and decide which size works for them. AI may narrow the choices, Johnson told TechCrunch. He added that many consumers would still want to experience the product themselves before spending that kind of money.

“AI will never be able to have you physically experience a product,” Johnson said. Instead, he expects agents to better inform consumers before they walk into a store. “They’ll just become more informed shoppers when they come to the store.”

Johnson’s conviction stems from a decision Apple made more than two decades ago. Apple’s physical stores, he said, were designed not only as places to buy Macs, but also as places where people could try products, learn how to use them, and return for help when something went wrong.

Some of those bets are revisited in Shop Different: How Retail Revealed Apple’s Genius, Johnson’s new book about building Apple’s retail operations alongside Steve Jobs. Competitors, he said, borrowed Apple’s glass-heavy design, open layouts, and even versions of the Genius Bar, but often missed the people.

“The secret sauce for Apple has always been its people, the people in the store, and how they treat the customer,” Johnson said.

Apple Store employees are not paid on commission, Johnson said, unlike the sales culture common across much of retail. The idea, he said, was to remove the pressure to sell and instead have employees figure out what a customer actually needed.

After leaving Apple, Johnson took over J.C. Penney in 2011 with an ambitious plan to reinvent the struggling department-store chain. He was ousted less than two years later after sales plunged.

Johnson now says he tried to change too much, too quickly, without bringing employees and customers along. Apple’s stores had effectively been a startup that evolved alongside the company’s products. J.C. Penney, on the other hand, was a turnaround that required a different approach.

“I applied a startup mentality to what needed to be a turnaround transformation,” he recalled.

Johnson later returned to the startup world, founding Enjoy Technology, an e-commerce company that brought technology products and setup services directly to customers’ homes. The startup filed for bankruptcy in 2022 and sold substantially all of its assets to Asurion.

For all his skepticism about how AI will reshape shopping, Johnson remains bullish on the technology itself. “I’m a real believer in AI. I’m an AI optimist,” he said.

He believes Jobs would have embraced AI, too, but not as a substitute for human judgment. “There’s no substitute for human intuition,” Johnson said, recalling Jobs’ belief in bringing smart people together to debate problems and find new ways of looking at them.

尽管硅谷正在斥资数十亿美元试图让人工智能（AI）智能体替我们购物，但这位开创了苹果零售店的元老认为，整个行业高估了人们会将多少购物环节转交给机器——并坚信实体零售店将继续蓬勃发展。

现年66岁的罗恩·约翰逊（Ron Johnson）此前就曾听过关于实体零售消亡的预言。2000年，在线购物刚刚兴起之际，他加入苹果公司负责打造其零售业务，并随后助力创建了一个零售店网络，该网络后来成为苹果销售产品和维系客户的核心枢纽。

“AI是一项能够改善在线购物体验的新技术，”约翰逊在一次采访中表示，“但我怀疑它是否真能改变我们的购物方式。”

约翰逊发表这一观点之际，全球部分最大的科技巨头正试图将AI更深地推向购物领域，押注智能体能够将我们寻找和购买商品的流程实现更高程度的自动化——这一概念通常被称为“智能体电商”（agentic commerce）。谷歌正通过其“通用商业协议”（Universal Commerce Protocol）来推进这一设想，该协议旨在帮助AI智能体带领消费者完成从发现商品到结账的全过程。与此同时，OpenAI正在将ChatGPT转变为一个购物目的地，用户无需离开聊天机器人，即可在其中检索、比价，甚至在某些情况下直接购买商品。

当被问及是否能想象有人完全不浏览网站或实体店，就让智能体全权挑选并购买一台价值1000美元或2000美元的笔记本电脑时，约翰逊明确表示：“坦率地说，没有人会这么做。”

他认为，购买笔记本电脑是一项过于个性化的决策，不能简单地委托给AI智能体。消费者希望感受它的重量、查看屏幕显示效果，并判断哪种尺寸适合自己。约翰逊向TechCrunch表示，AI或许能够缩小选择范围，但他补充道，许多消费者在掏出真金白银之前，依然会希望亲自体验产品。

“AI永远无法让你身临其境地体验产品，”约翰逊说。相反，他预计智能体将在消费者走进实体店之前提供更充分的信息。“当他们来到实体店时，他们只是变成了掌握更多信息的购物者。”

约翰逊的笃定源于苹果二十多年前做出的一个决策。他表示，苹果的实体店当初不仅被设计为购买Mac电脑的场所，而且还是供人们试用产品、学习使用方法，并在遇到问题时寻求帮助的地方。

约翰逊在记录其与史蒂夫·乔布斯（Steve Jobs）并肩打造苹果零售业务的新书《非同凡“想”的零售：零售如何彰显苹果的非凡智慧》（Shop Different: How Retail Revealed Apple’s Genius）中，重温了其中的部分决策。他提到，竞争对手借鉴了苹果大量采用玻璃的设计风格、开放式布局，甚至模仿了Genius Bar（天才吧），但往往忽略了核心要素——人。

“苹果的独门秘籍一直都在于人，在于零售店里的员工，以及他们对待顾客的方式，”约翰逊说。

约翰逊表示，与零售业普遍存在的销售文化不同，Apple Store的员工并不按销售提成拿薪酬。他说，这样设计的初衷是为了消除推销压力，转而让员工去真正弄清楚顾客需要什么。

离开苹果后，约翰逊于2011年执掌彭尼百货（J.C. Penney），并制定了一项雄心勃勃的重组计划，试图重振这家陷入困境的连锁百货公司。然而在销售额暴跌后，他在不到两年内便被免职。

约翰逊如今坦言，自己当时试图在没有带领员工和顾客同步跟上的情况下，过快地做出了过多的改变。苹果的零售店实际上是一项伴随公司产品一同成长的初创业务；而彭尼百货则是一场需要采取截然不同方式的企业扭亏战。

“我当时用初创企业的思维去应对了一场本需要扭亏转型的变革，”他回忆道。

约翰逊后来重返创业界，创立了电商公司Enjoy Technology，该公司直接将科技产品和安装调试服务送达客户家中。这家初创公司于2022年申请破产，并将其绝大部分资产出售给了Asurion。

尽管对AI将如何重塑购物持怀疑态度，约翰逊对该技术本身依然抱有信心。“我非常笃信AI，我是一个AI乐观主义者，”他说。

他认为乔布斯同样会接纳AI，但绝不会将其作为人类判断力的替代品。“人类的直觉是无法替代的，”约翰逊说，他回忆起乔布斯生前坚信要将聪明的人才聚在一起辩论问题、寻找看待问题的新视角。

Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

The Colorado River faces an ‘unprecedented’ drought as data centers demand more water.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Justine Calma

Amazon plans to spend $20 million on water conservation projects along the Colorado River, a crucial but dwindling water supply for 40 million people in the Western US.

The initiative comes as Amazon and other tech companies face mounting scrutiny over how much water their data centers use. Amazon has a goal of becoming water positive — replenishing more water than it uses — by the end of the decade. It recently disclosed some information about its water use, but we still have an incomplete picture of the company’s impact as a whole.

Amazon announced the launch of a Colorado River Basin Collaborative today, with a mission to “create one of the biggest corporate water conservation efforts for a single U.S. watershed.” It expects to raise $100 million over two years — including the $20 million investment from its own coffers — for water conservation efforts.

The Colorado River brings water to 40 million people

Stretching 1,400 miles, the Colorado River brings water to 40 million people across seven states in the Western US and and two states in Mexico. The waterway has faced “unprecedented” drought over the last 26 years, according to the US Bureau of Reclamation. Decades of overuse on top of human-caused climate change have exacerbated the problem. To cope, the US Department of the Interior finalized a plan in August imposing steep water cuts on Arizona, Nevada, and California.

As the first stop for most goods the US imports from Asia, California is home to more Amazon warehouses than any other state. In Orange County, California, Amazon pledged $2.2 million over the next three years to help detect and patch up leaks. That effort is ultimately supposed to conserve 189 million gallons of water each year, according to Amazon.

As part of the newly announced collaborative, other companies can contract independently with conservation projects they choose. The United Nations-backed Water Resilience Coalition will vet projects. Amazon is also joining the Water Resilience Coalition, which includes Microsoft, Meta, and other brands across a range of sectors.

Tech companies are facing waves of resistance against new AI data centers. AI was estimated to use between 312.5 billion and 764.6 billion liters of water in 2025, according to one estimate, about as much water as people consume globally in water bottles. In Arizona, Colorado River water cuts are expected to raise utility rates, and some residents fear data centers could make things worse.

In June, Amazon disclosed that its data centers used 2.5 billion gallons of water globally in 2025, including those it owns, leases, or shares. Data centers Amazon owns and operates directly reduced their water consumption by 2 percent in 2025 compared to the year prior, according to the company. It attributes gains to a 52 percent improvement in water efficiency since 2021. The company says it uses 0.12 liters of water per kilowatt-hour of electricity, claiming that’s about seven times more efficient than the industry average for data centers.

Amazon’s annual sustainability report shares water use per unit of power (l/kwh) for its data centers since 2021, but not the company’s total water use over that time period. Sustainability experts and environmental advocates caution against assessing a company’s sustainability by efficiency measurements alone. The more efficient a technology becomes, the more resources it might ultimately consume as companies start using it more, according to an economic concept called Jevons paradox. That makes it important to track how much water a company is using overall, as well as how much it needs in each place it operates during demand peaks when supply is most limited.

For comparison, Microsoft’s latest sustainability report discloses its data centers’ total water use since 2020, while Google’s report shares water use for global operations since 2021 with a breakdown by location. All three tech giants have had to abandon data center projects after facing community opposition, Reuters reports. Unlike other tech companies, Amazon’s warehouses also have a massive physical footprint that isn’t reflected in the company’s data center disclosures.

A Guardian investigation in 2025 alleges that Amazon obscured how much water the company uses by deciding not to account for how much it takes to generate electricity, considered a “secondary” water use. Concerned about “reputational risk,” executives decided to only address “primary” water use at its facilities when calculating progress toward sustainability goals. The numbers Amazon recently shared about its data center water use also exclude water consumption stemming from electricity generation.

While data centers often use water for cooling systems, a majority of a data center’s water footprint stems from this “secondary use.” Power plants need water to cool equipment and turn turbines using steam, and in 2021, Amazon used 10.5 billion gallons (39.7 billion liters) of water in 2021, according to the Guardian report citing an internal leaked document. That’s about as much as 95,000 US households consume.

In an email to The Verge, Amazon spokesperson Margaret Callahan says the Guardian report “relied on cherry-picked data from an outdated document that misrepresents our water strategy — making the conclusions fundamentally wrong and misleading” and that a “document’s existence doesn’t guarantee its accuracy or finality.”

Callahan didn’t provide more data on how much water Amazon has used in total over the years. She pointed out that the company is 75 percent toward its goal of becoming water positive, returning 3 gallons for every 4 that it used last year.

In its announcement today, Kara Hurst, chief sustainability officer at Amazon, compares the new Colorado River initiative to the company’s previous climate targets.

”Through the Climate Pledge, we’ve seen what happens when companies tackle a problem together: progress accelerates. We’re bringing that same model to the Colorado River because water and climate are deeply connected,” Hurst says.

Amazon’s carbon footprint, however, grew 16 percent in 2025 — a trend happening across the tech industry as companies race to make advances in AI.

当前，亚马逊等科技巨头的数据中心耗水量正面临日益严格的审查，该倡议正是在此背景下推出的。亚马逊定下目标，力争在本十年末实现“水资源正效益”（water positive）——即补充的水量超过其消耗的水量。该公司近期披露了部分用水信息，但我们对其总体环境影响依然缺乏全貌认识。

亚马逊今天宣布启动“科罗拉多河流域协作机制”（Colorado River Basin Collaborative），其使命是“打造针对美国单一流域规模最大的企业节水举措之一”。该协作机制预计在两年内筹集1亿美元资金用于节水工作，其中包括亚马逊自掏腰包投入的2000万美元。

科罗拉多河为4000万人提供水源

科罗拉多河全长1400英里，为美国西部七个州以及墨西哥两个州的4000万人提供用水。根据美国垦务局的数据，在过去26年里，该水道遭遇了“史无前例”的干旱。人为导致的气候变化加上数十年的过度开采，令这一问题雪上加霜。为应对危机，美国内政部于8月敲定了一项计划，对亚利桑那州、内华达州和加利福尼亚州实施大幅削减供水配额。

加利福尼亚州是美国从亚洲进口大部分商品的首站，其拥有的亚马逊仓库数量位居各州之首。在加州奥兰治县，亚马逊承诺在未来三年内投入220万美元，协助检测并修补漏水管道。据亚马逊称，此项举措预计每年最终将节约1.89亿加仑的水。

作为这项新宣布协作机制的一部分，其他公司可以根据自主选择与各类保护项目独立签约。联合国支持的“水资源韧性联盟”（Water Resilience Coalition）将负责审核项目。亚马逊也加入了该联盟，联盟成员还包括微软、Meta以及其他多个行业的品牌。

科技公司正面临针对新建人工智能数据中心的一波波抵制浪潮。据一项估算，2025年人工智能的耗水量预计将在3125亿至7646亿升之间，大致相当于全球人口饮用瓶装水的总量。在亚利桑那州，科罗拉多河供水量的削减预计将推高公用事业公费费率，部分居民担心数据中心可能会让局势进一步恶化。

今年6月，亚马逊披露其全球范围内的数据中心（包括其自有、租赁或共用的数据中心）在2025年共消耗了25亿加仑的水。该公司表示，与上一年相比，其直接拥有并运营的数据中心在2025年的耗水量减少了2%。亚马逊将此归功于自2021年以来水利用效率提升了52%。该公司称其每消耗一度电（千瓦时）仅使用0.12升水，并宣称其效率比数据中心行业平均水平高出约七倍。

亚马逊的年度可持续发展报告公布了自2021年以来其数据中心每单位电力的耗水量（升/千瓦时），但并未透露该公司在这一时期的总耗水量。可持续发展专家和环保倡导者警告称，切勿仅凭效率指标来评估一家公司的可持续性。经济学中有一个名为“杰文斯悖论”（Jevons paradox）的理论：一种技术效率越高，随着企业加大其使用规模，最终可能消耗更多的资源。因此，追踪一家公司的总体用水量，以及在供应最为紧张的用水高峰期其各个运营地点的实际需求量，显得至关重要。

作为对比，微软最新的可持续发展报告披露了其数据中心自2020年以来的总耗水量，而谷歌的报告则按地点细分公开了自2021年以来其全球业务的耗水量。路透社报道称，在遭遇社区反对后，这三家科技巨头均不得不放弃过部分数据中心项目。与其他科技公司不同的是，亚马逊的仓库也拥有庞大的实体占地面积，而这一部分的用水情况并未在其数据中心披露报告中体现。

《卫报》在2025年的一项调查指控称，亚马逊决定不计入发电所需的耗水量（这被视为“间接/二次”用水），从而掩盖了公司的实际总耗水量。出于对“声誉风险”的担忧，高管们在计算可持续发展目标进展时，决定仅统计其设施内部的“直接/一次”用水。亚马逊近期分享的数据中心用水数据同样排除了发电产生的耗水量。

虽然数据中心通常使用水来冷却系统，但其水足迹的大部分实际上来自这种“间接用水”。发电厂需要用水来冷却设备并利用蒸汽驱动涡轮机；《卫报》援引一份内部泄露的文件报道称，2021年亚马逊的用水量达到了105亿加仑（约397亿升）。这大约相当于9.5万个美国家庭的年消耗量。

在发给The Verge的一封电子邮件中，亚马逊发言人玛格丽特·卡拉汉（Margaret Callahan）表示，《卫报》的报道“依赖于一份过时文件中的断章取义数据，曲解了我们的水资源战略，导致其结论从根本上是错误且具有误导性的”，并称“一份文件的存在并不能保证其准确性或最终确定性”。

卡拉汉并未提供更多关于亚马逊多年来累计总耗水量的数据。她指出，该公司在实现“水资源正效益”目标的道路上已完成75%，去年每消耗4加仑水即可回补3加仑。

在今天的公告中，亚马逊首席可持续发展官卡拉·赫斯特（Kara Hurst）将这项新的科罗拉多河倡议与公司以往的气候目标进行了类比。

赫斯特表示：“通过《气候宣言》（Climate Pledge），我们见证了企业携手解决问题时所产生的效应：进展得以加速。我们将把同样的模式带到科罗拉多河，因为水资源与气候密不可分。”

然而，2025年亚马逊的碳足迹增长了16%——随着各大企业竞相推进人工智能技术，这一趋势正席卷整个科技行业。

aiStories.title: 是间谍印记，而非水印
aiStories.fullContent:
Watermarks that spy on users are no mere watermarks

There’s a sneaky new evolution of the “watermark”, let’s call it — the spymark.

A watermark is a visible mark embedded in a physical or digital medium to verify authenticity or assert ownership.

A spymark is a hidden signal that makes your work traceable without your knowledge or consent.

Google SynthID is a spymark that embeds secret hidden signals “imperceptible to humans” (Google’s own words) into images, audio, text, and video. This signal can encode database identifiers that map to your identity. Your user records, full name, IP addresses, date of birth, physical addresses, political party affiliation, and more.

Google’s SynthID-Image paper reports that its SynthID-O variant can encode a 136-bit payload in a 512x512-pixel image. That is enough room for a 64-bit database identifier, with 72 bits left for error correction.

SynthID was not the first spymark system designed, and it’s hardly the only one under active development. OpenAI and many other tech companies are developing these systems at scale. These companies claim spymarking can help identify AI-generated content, yet they’ve gone beyond simple watermarking and built in robust tracking mechanisms. Social media, content production tools, and smartphones may soon find themselves filled with spymarking algorithms that sneak these signals into everything you publish.

For example, images can be invisibly altered in their frequency domain to carry tracking information such as database IDs linked to users:

A smaller version of Mochi’s photo contains a real toy watermark: ID 173, encoded through subtle pixel changes. Compare the original and marked image, animate the amplified differences, and decode the ID from the PNG. The associated author and timestamp are fictional.

“Watermark” has become a catchall for historical marks of authenticity, banknote security features, copyright overlays, and hidden tracking signals in our media. That last usage obscures the privacy risk that some forms of modern “watermarks” have become.

Most people tire of the discourse on privacy. It’s complex, repetitive, and seems irrelevant to the typical day-to-day routine of the average citizen. We can’t keep explaining the technicalities behind statistical tracking tools each and every time we need to communicate these concepts to people and expect them to pay attention.

“To speak the name is to control the thing.” — Ursula K. Le Guin, The Rule of Names

With a simple change of terminology we can put the privacy concern up front, cementing this issue in the conversation forever:

Now we get to disambiguate friendly watermarks from concerning new technology while leveraging the familiar etymology. It collapses a technical communication salient and gains us a lot of ground with just one new word. It’s clear, coherent, and straight to the point.

No more wasting energy establishing the basic facts. The privacy concern is built into the word.

“Spymark” is a privacy Rumpelstiltskin.

Here are a few more forms of spymarks so you can better familiarize yourself.

Audio spymarks operate using principles similar to image spymarks, and they are typically inaudible. Some methods make minute changes to the audio waveform in the time domain; others modify features in the frequency domain, and some combine both approaches. These methods can encode data, including identifiers linked to personal information:

Compare spectrograms of the same LJ Speech excerpt unwatermarked and with Timbre, AudioSeal, WavMark, FSVC, Patchwork, or Norm-Space. The authors’ original plots are linked below.

Spectrograms from Wen et al. (2025), SoK: How Robust is Audio Watermarking in Generative AI models? · Original samples. Plots retain the authors’ original scales.

These schemes are engineered to be robust. They can often survive compression or re-encoding.

These tools are already proliferating, and in fact they predated generative AI and the push to watermark generative media. The open source spymarking tool audiowmark originated in 2018 and can hide 128-bit payloads in audio and protect them with a secret AES key, preventing users without the key from decoding them.

You can even encode personal information invisibly into text! SynthID steers word choices to create a detectable statistical pattern that can encode a tracking payload:

An illustrative encoding: eight word choices represent eight bits. The binary value 10101101 gives database ID 173, which can point to a record containing an author and timestamp. These are fictional examples, not a SynthID decoder.

Watermarks remain easy for the user to spot and are typically not nefarious.

Sometimes watermarks deter counterfeiting:

Sometimes watermarks claim ownership:

And sometimes they’re just annoying:

But these watermarks don’t track you.

Printer tracking dots, on the other hand, are an early example of spymarks, dating back to the 1980s:

We need to be clear that spymarks are a form of metadata you have limited knowledge of and control over, and that their purpose is entirely antagonistic to you.

Metadata such as the EXIF tags in photos and the ID3 tags in MP3 files are standardized, well-documented fields. While EXIF can expose sensitive data such as GPS coordinates, these standardized fields can be inspected, edited, and removed from files you control.

Inspect editable EXIF and ID3 metadata in two tabs. EXIF shows fictional camera-maker, model, and author tags in a JPEG metadata segment; ID3 shows an MP3’s title, artist, and album. Hover or tap the bytes for explanations. These samples contain metadata only.

You can strip standard metadata tags out of your files. Unfortunately, a spymark signal embedded in pixels, audio, or word choices is invisible to you and can remain in your files even after you edit them.

Furthermore, whereas tags are helpful for maintaining information such as song titles or a photo’s exposure settings, spymarks encode user-tracking identifiers that are entirely opaque and useless to you. These signals can survive metadata removal and some edits, allowing marked copies to remain traceable as they circulate.

It’s hard to imagine the future where we can’t even trust our own files. And the sad thing is that this has already started.

Spymarks are certainly not great for whistleblowers or anyone who doesn’t want to be persecuted for their words or affiliations. No matter where you stand on whatever issues, spymarks can be used against you and those you care about.

Imagine a future where every device is attested and every social media post carries an account-linked spymark. Where every file or post served to you for sharing has spymarks embedded within. Combined with account records and observations of where copies appear, these identifiers can help reconstruct how content spreads. In this world, it would be dangerously easy to hunt down anyone from a JPEG or a tweet. Or track the web of humans through which “dangerous ideas” flow.

That future lies halfway between now and 1984. So let’s stay off that timeline, shall we?

Call a spymark what it is. A spy tool used to spy on you and everyone you interact with.

A hidden signal embedded in media to trace its origin, tools, or distribution history without the user’s meaningful control.

“The spymarks tied each copy to a different recipient.”

spymarked; spymarking; spymarks

To embed a spymark in a file or piece of media.

“The social network spymarks every uploaded image.”

The practice of embedding spymarks.

“The platform introduced spymarking without telling its users.”

Containing a spymark.

“Removing the file’s metadata still left the image spymarked.”
aiStories.fullTranslation:
监视用户的水印绝非普通水印。
“水印”出现了一种狡黠的新演变，我们不妨称之为——间谍印记（spymark）。
水印是嵌入在物理或数字介质中的可见标记，用于验证真实性或宣告所有权。
而间谍印记是一种隐藏信号，可以在你不知情或未同意的情况下使你的作品具有可追溯性。
谷歌的 SynthID 就是一种间谍印记，它将“人类无法察觉”（谷歌官方用语）的秘密隐藏信号嵌入图像、音频、文本和视频中。该信号可以编码映射到你身份的数据库标识符：你的用户记录、全名、IP 地址、出生日期、实际住址、党派偏好等。
谷歌关于 SynthID-Image 的论文指出，其 SynthID-O 变体可以在 512x512 像素的图像中编码 136 位有效载荷。这足以容纳一个 64 位的数据库标识符，并留下 72 位用于纠错。
SynthID 并不是第一个设计出的间谍印记系统，也绝非唯一正在积极开发的系统。OpenAI 和许多其他科技公司正在大规模开发这类系统。这些公司声称间谍印记有助于识别 AI 生成的内容，但他们已经超越了简单的水印制作，内置了强大的追踪机制。社交媒体、内容生产工具和智能手机可能很快就会充斥着间谍印记算法，将这些信号悄悄植入你发布的每一项内容中。
例如，图像可以在频域进行肉眼不可见的修改，以承载与用户关联的数据库 ID 等追踪信息：
Mochi 照片的较小版本包含一个真实的玩具水印：通过细微的像素变化编码的 ID 173。对比原始图像和标记图像，动态放大差异，并从 PNG 中解码出 ID。相关的作者和时间戳均为虚构。
“水印”已经成为一个总称，涵盖了历史上的真实性标记、钞票防伪特征、版权浮层以及我们媒体中的隐藏追踪信号。这最后一种用法掩盖了某些形式的现代“水印”所演变而成的隐私风险。
大多数人对隐私议题的讨论感到厌倦。它复杂、重复，而且对于普通民众的日常例行琐事而言显得无关痛痒。我们不能指望每次需要向人们传达这些概念时，都要不断解释统计追踪工具背后的技术细节并期望他们保持关注。
“能直呼其名，方能掌控其物。”——厄休拉·K·勒古恩，《地海传奇：名言之规》（The Rule of Names）
只要简单更改术语，我们就能将隐私担忧置于首位，从而将这一问题永远确立在公共讨论中：
现在，我们可以借助熟悉的词源学，将友好的水印与令人担忧的新技术区分开来。仅仅通过一个新词，它就化解了技术传播上的阻碍，并为我们争取到了极大的主动权。它清晰、连贯且直击要害。
不必再浪费精力去陈述基本事实。隐私隐患已经内置于这个词汇之中。
“间谍印记”（Spymark）就是隐私领域的侏儒怪（Rumpelstiltskin）。
以下是间谍印记的另外几种形式，以便你更好地熟悉。
音频间谍印记的工作原理与图像间谍印记类似，且通常是听不见的。某些方法在时域对音频波形进行微小的更改；其他方法在频域修改特征，还有一些方法结合了这两种方式。这些方法可以对数据进行编码，包括与个人信息关联的标识符：
对比未经水印处理与使用 Timbre、AudioSeal、WavMark、FSVC、Patchwork 或 Norm-Space 处理后的同一段 LJ Speech 节选语谱图。作者的原始图表链接见下方。
语谱图引自 Wen 等人（2025年），《SoK：生成式 AI 模型中的音频水印有多鲁棒？》（SoK: How Robust is Audio Watermarking in Generative AI models?）· 原始样本。图表保留了作者的原始比例尺。
这些方案经过工程设计，具有极强的鲁棒性。它们通常能在压缩或重新编码后存活下来。
这些工具已经在迅速扩散，事实上，它们的出现早于生成式 AI 以及为生成式媒体打水印的浪潮。开源间谍印记工具 audiowmark 始于 2018 年，可以在音频中隐藏 128 位有效载荷，并使用秘密 AES 密钥对其进行保护，防止没有密钥的用户解码。
你甚至可以将个人信息隐形地编码到文本中！SynthID 会引导词语选择，以创造一种可被检测到的统计模式，该模式能够编码追踪载荷：
一个示例性编码：八个词语选择代表八个比特。二进制值 10101101 得出数据库 ID 173，该 ID 可以指向包含作者和时间戳的记录。这些是虚构示例，并非 SynthID 解码器。
水印对于用户来说仍然易于察觉，且通常没有恶意。
有时水印可以防伪：
有时水印用于宣告所有权：
有时它们只是令人烦恼：
但这些水印不会追踪你。
另一方面，打印机追踪黄点是间谍印记的早期范例，可以追溯到 20 世纪 80 年代：
我们需要明确，间谍印记是一种你对其知之甚少且几乎无法控制的元数据形式，而且其目的完全是对抗你的。
像照片中的 EXIF 标签和 MP3 文件中的 ID3 标签这样的元数据是标准化、记录完备的字段。尽管 EXIF 可能会暴露 GPS 坐标等敏感数据，但这些标准化字段可以在受你控制的文件中进行检查、编辑和删除。
可以在两个选项卡中检查可编辑的 EXIF 和 ID3 元数据。EXIF 在 JPEG 元数据段中显示虚构的相机制造商、型号和作者标签；ID3 显示 MP3 的标题、艺术家和专辑。将光标悬停或轻触字节可查看说明。这些示例仅包含元数据。
你可以从文件中剥离标准的元数据标签。遗憾的是，嵌入在像素、音频或词语选择中的间谍印记信号对你而言是不可见的，即使你在编辑文件后，它们仍可能留在文件中。
此外，标签有助于维护歌曲标题或照片曝光设置等信息，而间谍印记编码的用户追踪标识符对你来说完全不透明且毫无用处。这些信号在移除元数据和进行部分编辑后仍可留存，从而使带有标记的副本在流通过程中始终保持可追踪。
很难想象一个连我们自己的文件都无法信任的未来。而令人悲伤的是，这一切已经开始了。
间谍印记对于吹哨人或任何不希望因其言论或归属而遭受迫害的人来说，绝对不是好事。无论你在任何问题上持何种立场，间谍印记都可以被用来对抗你以及你所关心的人。

想象这样一个未来：每台设备都经过认证，每一条社交媒体帖子都携带与账户绑定的间谍印记（spymark）。提供给你供分享的每一个文件或帖子都嵌入了间谍印记。结合账户记录以及对副本出现位置的追踪观察，这些标识符可以帮助重构内容的传播路径。在这样一个世界里，仅仅凭借一张 JPEG 图片或一条推文就能极其危险地轻松定位追查任何人。抑或是追踪“危险思想”在其中流转的人际网络。

那个未来正处在当下与《1984》之间。所以，让我们避开那条时间线，好吗？

直面间谍印记的本质吧。它就是一种用来监视你以及与你互动的每一个人的间谍工具。

一种嵌入在媒体中的隐藏信号，用于在用户缺乏有效控制权的情况下追踪其来源、生成工具或分发历史。

“间谍印记将每个副本与不同的接收者关联起来。”

spymarked（带有间谍印记的）；spymarking（间谍印记植入）；spymarks（间谍印记，动词第三人称单数/名词复数）

将间谍印记嵌入文件或媒体片段中。

“该社交网络会对每张上传的图片嵌入间谍印记。”

嵌入间谍印记的做法。

“该平台在未告知用户的情况下引入了间谍印记机制。”

含有间谍印记。

“即使删除了文件的元数据，该图片仍带有间谍印记。”
