trendStories.fullContent:
People in the UK are more interested in oral health than ever - and you can now buy prebiotic toothpastes and brushes that cost up to £600. Yet we remain in the midst of a serious dental crisis

A December 1969 report from the consumer magazine Which? explored a relatively new gadget that, it predicted, many people would be giving as Christmas presents: the electric toothbrush. For those who hadn’t yet seen one, the magazine described it as “not that much different in principle from an ordinary brush – you have a stick with a brush on the end. The difference is that an electric one moves the brush head for you”. Progress indeed.

Nearly six decades on, electric toothbrushes can do a lot more than merely jiggle, offering multiple speeds and movement sensors for real-time tracking of where you’ve brushed – some even promise gum-massage or tongue-cleaning modes. Prices range from about £25 for a basic Oral B model to £599.99 for a Philips Sonicare model that gives “smart coverage feedback”. The latest super-toothbrush – a mere £419.99 – features a camera and a built-in water jet to clean between teeth, using AI to identify gaps. Created by Dyson, it’s still, essentially, a stick with a brush on the end (although there is another toothbrush on the market that’s shaped like a mouthguard, with individual brushes, that claims to clean your teeth in 20 seconds).
trendStories.fullTranslation:
英国人对口腔健康的关注度达到前所未有的高度——如今人们甚至可以买到益生菌牙膏以及售价高达600英镑的牙刷。然而，我们依然深陷严重的牙科医疗危机之中。

消费者杂志《Which?》在1969年12月的一份报告中探讨了一种相对新颖的小物件，并预测许多人会将其作为圣诞礼物相赠：那就是电动牙刷。对于那些尚未见过这种产品的人，该杂志将其描述为“原理上与普通牙刷相差无几——也就是一根末端带有刷毛的棍子。区别在于电动牙刷能自动替你摆动刷头”。这确实算得上是一种进步。

近60年后的今天，电动牙刷的功能已远不止是简单的震颤，它们提供多种转速档位，并配备运动传感器以实时追踪刷牙路径——有些甚至宣称具备牙龈按摩或舌苔清洁模式。其售价从基础款欧乐-B（Oral B）的约25英镑，到能够提供“智能覆盖范围反馈”的飞利浦索尼克（Philips Sonicare）型号的599.99英镑不等。最新款超级牙刷售价“只要”419.99英镑，它配备了摄像头和内置水流冲洗装置，可通过AI识别牙缝以清洁齿间。这款由戴森（Dyson）打造的产品，在本质上依然是一根末端带有刷毛的棍子（尽管市面上还有另一款形状酷似护齿牙套、带有独立刷头的牙刷，声称能在20秒内完成清洁）。

trendStories.title: 要闻：1996年5月，当我正在撰写我的第二篇 JavaWorld 文章《类文件的生活方式》（"The Class Fi
trendStories.fullContent:
In May of 1996, as I was working on my second JavaWorld article, "The Class File Lifestyle," I became curious about the Java class file's magic number, 0xCAFEBABE. The first four bytes of every Java class file are specified to be 0xCAFEBABE, a magic number that can help tools quickly differentiate likely class files from non class files. Wondering whether any deep meaning lurked behind this value, I posted the following question to the comp.lang.java newsgroup.

The first 4 bytes of every Java class file has the magic value 0xCAFEBABE. I am curious. Does anyone know how this value was chosen? Does anyone who doesn't know want to venture a guess?

I have heard why before, but the answer seems to have long since been deleted from my e-mail archives. I, too, would like to know why. why?

Well, they presumably had to pick something as their magic number to identify class files, and there's a limit to how many Java or coffee related words you can come up with using just the letters A-F :-)

Matthew Travis wrote:

Well, the file has to start with *some* magic number (or string) to make it easy to recognize as a valid class file and not something else.

As to why the magic number is 3405691582 (0xCAFEBABE), well my guess is that (a) 32-bit magic numbers are easier to handle and more likely to be unique, and (b) the Java team wanted something with the Java-coffee metaphor, and since there's no 'J' or 'V' in hexadecimal, settled for something with CAFE in it. I guess they figured "CAFE BABE" was sexier than something like "A FAB CAFE" or "CAFE FACE", and definitely didn't like the implications of "CAFE A FAD" (or worse, "A BAD CAFE").

(BTW, of course they're far from the first to use hex digits to spell out meaningful words in their magic numbers. Twenty-something years ago the Burroughs B6700 initialized its "uninitialized" memory of 48-bit words to 0xBADBADBADBAD.)

Alastair Mayer wrote:

it. I guess they figured "CAFE BABE" was sexier than something like "A FAB CAFE" or "CAFE FACE", and definitely didn't like the implications of "CAFE A FAD" (or worse, "A BAD CAFE").

Don't know why I missed this before, but they *could* have used the number 12648430, if you choose to read the hex zeros as the letter 'O'. That gives you 0xC0FFEE, or 0x00C0FFEE to specify all 32 bits. OO COFFEE? Object Oriented, of course... :-)

Well, the file has to start with *some* magic number (or string)to make it easy to recognize as a valid class file and not something else.

Back when I was a mere child, I was helping a numerical analyst debug a program. The S/360 core dump (anyone remember hex matrixes!) finally yielded up the culpret: a very out-of-range floating point value.

The first three digits were 0xBAD.

I had a hell of a time convincing that guy that it was purely a coincidence!

David N. Smith wrote:

A canonical (that is, referred to explicitly in "The New Hacker's Dictionary") "bogus value" to stick in places that need an easily-identifiable bogus value is 0xDEADBEEF.

On the Macintosh, which lacks protected memory, a popular thing to do is to stick some magic number into location 0 so that dereferencing a null pointer or handle will crash immediately. Long ago, a friend used the ASCII value of 'NIL!' for the purpose, but time and some real thought about what a good value on the Macintosh really was eventually led to 0x50FFC001, which is a flawless Mac crasher value (for at least three reasons that are left as an exercise to the reader) but unfortunately isn't a cool legible value. --

I originally saw 0xCAFEBABE as a magic number used by NeXTSTEP. NX used "fat binaries", which were basically binaries for different platforms stuck together in one executable file. If you were running on NX Intel, it would run the Intel binary; if on HP, it would run the HP binary. 0xCAFEBABE was the magic number to distinguish either the Intel or the Motorola binaries ( can't remember which ).

Seems that Sun carried it over ...

Vivian Man Cheng wrote:

I originally saw 0xCAFEBABE as a magic number used by NeXTSTEP.

Strange but true... 0xfeedface is for moto and 0xcafebabe for intel. What about Sun and HP though?

Do you think it's copyrighted or trademarked to NeXT? :-)

Since the word babe is pretty synonmous with chick, I doubt you'll find any _deep_ meaning here. When I hear "CafeBabe" I think of a typical Coffee Grrl: nose peirced, minimum one tatoo, hair dyed black, hate the world the government and parents, and is rather attractive in a necro sort of way.

But that's what I get from it. It could be a tribute to the waitress who served Sun's Java team at their favorite bean hole. Or, maybe it one of the few things they could spell with A-F, and CAFEBEEF or DEADCAFE wasn't nearly as nice sounding to them as CAFEBABE.

Who knows. You could write them.

And don't forget the old IBM machines that used 0xDEADBEEF for the same purpose. Using uninitialized memory is still called a "dead beef error" in some circles (at least among programmers old enough to remember that).

AIX on RS6000 still uses 0xdeadbeaf to represent unitialized storage.

Strangely enough the magic number for .class files was chosen long before the name Java was ever uttered in reference to this language. We were looking for something fun, unique and easy to remember. 0xcafebabe was better than the second runner-up, 0xdeadbabe. :-)

It is only a coincidence that the oblique reference to the cute barristas at Peet's Coffee was foreshadowing for the name Java.

Patrick Naughton wrote:

0xdeadbabe is used at the start of all IRIX arena files! So good thing you didn't use it! ;)

Simon Bennett wrote:

and a debugging solaris kernel puts 0xCAFEFEED into all kmemfree() blocks. --b
trendStories.fullTranslation:
1996年5月，当我正在撰写我的第二篇 JavaWorld 文章《类文件的生活方式》（"The Class File Lifestyle"）时，我对 Java 类文件的魔数 0xCAFEBABE 产生了好奇。每个 Java 类文件的前4个字节都被规定为 0xCAFEBABE，这是一个有助于工具快速将潜在的类文件与非类文件区分开来的魔数。出于对这个数值背后是否隐藏着某种深层含义的好奇，我在 comp.lang.java 新闻组发布了以下问题：

每个 Java 类文件的前4个字节都有魔数值 0xCAFEBABE。我很好奇，有人知道这个值是怎么选出来的吗？不知道的人有人想猜一猜吗？

我以前听过原因，但答案似乎早就从我的电子邮件归档中删除了。我也很想知道为什么。为什么？

好吧，他们想必得选点什么作为魔数来标识类文件，而在仅使用字母 A 到 F 的情况下，你能想到的与 Java 或咖啡相关的词汇是很有限的 :-)

Matthew Travis 写道：
好吧，文件必须以*某个*魔数（或字符串）开头，以便轻松识别为有效类文件，而不是其他东西。
至于为什么魔数是 3405691582 (0xCAFEBABE)，嗯，我的猜测是：(a) 32位魔数更容易处理，且更有可能是唯一的；(b) Java 团队想要一些带有 Java-咖啡隐喻的东西，由于十六进制中没有“J”或“V”，他们就折中选了带有 CAFE 的词。我猜他们觉得“CAFE BABE”比“A FAB CAFE”或“CAFE FACE”之类的更性感，而且绝对不喜欢“CAFE A FAD”（或者更糟的“A BAD CAFE”）所带来的含义。
（顺便说一句，他们当然远非第一批在魔数中使用十六进制数字拼写出有意义单词的人。二十多年前，Burroughs B6700 将其48位字长的“未初始化”内存初始化为 0xBADBADBADBAD。）

Alastair Mayer 写道：
它。我猜他们觉得“CAFE BABE”比“A FAB CAFE”或“CAFE FACE”之类的更性感，而且绝对不喜欢“CAFE A FAD”（或者更糟的“A BAD CAFE”）所带来的含义。
不知道我之前为什么忽略了这个，但如果把十六进制的 0 读作字母 'O' 的话，他们*本来可以*使用数字 12648430。这样就得到了 0xC0FFEE，或者指定全部32位为 0x00C0FFEE。OO COFFEE？当然是面向对象（Object Oriented）…… :-)

好吧，文件必须以*某个*魔数（或字符串）开头，以便轻松识别为有效类文件，而不是其他东西。

当我还是个小孩子时，我帮一位数值分析师调试程序。S/360 核心转储（core dump，还有人记得十六进制矩阵吗！）终于揪出了罪魁祸首：一个极度超出范围的浮点值。
前三位数字是 0xBAD。
我费了九牛二虎之力才让那家伙相信这纯属巧合！

David N. Smith 写道：
在需要填入容易识别的假值的地方，一个经典的（即在《新黑客词典》中被明确引用的）“伪值”是 0xDEADBEEF。

在缺乏内存保护的 Macintosh 上，一种流行的做法是在位置 0 填入某个魔数，这样解引用空指针或句柄时就会立即崩溃。很久以前，一位朋友出于这个目的使用了 'NIL!' 的 ASCII 值，但经过深思熟虑以及对 Macintosh 上真正合适数值的探索，最终找到了 0x50FFC001——这是一个完美的 Mac 崩溃值（至少有三个原因，留作给读者的思考题），但遗憾的是它并不是一个酷炫易读的值。--

我最初是在 NeXTSTEP 中看到使用 0xCAFEBABE 作为魔数的。NX 使用了“胖二进制”（fat binaries），本质上就是将不同平台的二进制文件打包在一个可执行文件中。如果你在 NX Intel 上运行，它就会运行 Intel 二进制文件；如果是在 HP 上，就会运行 HP 二进制文件。0xCAFEBABE 就是用来区分 Intel 还是 Motorola 二进制文件的魔数（记不清是哪一个了）。
看来 Sun 把它沿用过来了……

Vivian Man Cheng 写道：
我最初看到 0xCAFEBABE 是作为 NeXTSTEP 使用的魔数。
奇怪但千真万确……0xfeedface 用于摩托罗拉（moto），0xcafebabe 用于英特尔（intel）。不过 Sun 和 HP 呢？
你觉得它会被 NeXT 注册版权或商标吗？:-)

既然“babe”这个词基本上就是“chick”（小妞）的同义词，我怀疑你在这里找不到任何*深层*含义。当我听到“CafeBabe”时，我想到的就是一个典型的“咖啡女孩”：穿鼻环、至少有一处文身、头发染成黑色、厌恶世界、政府和父母，有一种偏哥特/病态式的吸引力。
但这是我的理解。它也可能是向在 Sun 的 Java 团队常去的小咖啡馆里为他们服务的女服务员致敬。或者，也许这是他们仅用 A-F 能拼出的少数词汇之一，而且在他们看来，CAFEBEEF 或 DEADCAFE 听起来远不如 CAFEBABE 顺耳。
谁知道呢。你可以写信问他们。

别忘了老式 IBM 机器出于同样的目的使用了 0xDEADBEEF。在某些圈子里（至少在那些年纪足以记住那段历史的程序员中），使用未初始化内存仍然被称为“死牛肉错误”（dead beef error）。
RS6000 上的 AIX 仍然使用 0xdeadbeaf 来表示未初始化的存储空间。

说来也怪，.class 文件的魔数早在“Java”这个名字被用来指代该语言之前很久就被选定了。我们当时在寻找某种有趣、独特且容易记住的东西。0xcafebabe 比第二顺位候选者 0xdeadbabe 更好。:-)
隐约指代皮爷咖啡（Peet's Coffee）可爱的咖啡师，并作为“Java”这个名字的预兆，这纯属巧合。

Patrick Naughton 写道：
0xdeadbabe 被用在所有 IRIX arena 文件的开头！所以幸好你们没用它！;)

Simon Bennett 写道：
而调试版 Solaris 内核会将 0xCAFEFEED 写入所有的 kmemfree() 内存块中。--b

trendStories.fullContent:
Holdout juror in Clancy’s case, Michael Desronvil, sided with the prosecutors, arguing that Clancy knew what she was doing when she killed her three young children

Lawyers for Lindsay Clancy have asked a judge to investigate the conduct of the lone juror who wanted to convict the mother from Massachusetts of murder in the deaths of her three children.

In a motion filed Friday but made public Monday, Clancy’s lawyers asked the court to question the juror about his alleged use of a cellphone during deliberations, his truthfulness on a questionnaire that prospective jurors filled out before the trial began and his truthfulness when jurors were questioned by the judge a day before the trial ended.
trendStories.fullTranslation:
克兰西案中持异议的陪审员迈克尔·德斯朗维尔（Michael Desronvil）支持检方立场，认为克兰西在杀害其三名年幼子女时清楚知道自己在做什么。

林赛·克兰西（Lindsay Clancy）的辩护律师已请求法官调查这名唯一的陪审员的行为，该陪审员此前坚持主张判处这位来自马萨诸塞州的母亲在三名子女死亡案中犯有谋杀罪。

在周五提交并于周一公开的一份动议中，克兰西的律师请求法庭就该陪审员在陪审团审议期间涉嫌使用手机的情况、其在审判开始前候选陪审员填写的问卷中的陈述真实性，以及在审判结束前一天法官对其进行问话时的诚实度进行质询。
